#2123 1 2005-03-04T10:13:25Z sweep
Right, all I ask is you post a list of things that make a level great for you, and a list of things that make them bad. The major factors: turnons/turnoffs. Good/bad. Simple. It'd be nice for some reasons, too.

+Gausses. I love gausses! They're not too hard to beat, but they can be used in a level to be hard. They're very versatile, and I don't find them too irritating.
+Really tiny loading times. I love it when someone creates a really good level with really small loading times. Equally, I love it when they create a really compact level anyway.
+New concepts. Anything breaking the boundaries.
+Difficulty switches. Someone did something the other day, on a level that was unfortunately poor - but one part of it I really liked. At the beginning, there were two switches, you went for one or the other first. One was for a hard difficulty level, the other for easy. I loved this. And I demand more.

-Rocket thingies. I suck at beating them. Sure, I'm not saying they're all bad (they have their uses, I use them sometimes), but as a general rule it makes me automatically think 'aw'.
-Long load times. I'm really tetchy about this. Especially if it's unnessasery. DDAs, fair enough - you only watch them once (usually), so it's not irritating. But I hate long load times.
-Requests. Grrr. I really hate this. 'Please don't rate my map' - then don't post it on NUMA! 'If you get lag, delete some objects!' - no! It's your map! If you want me to play it, you do it!
-Survival maps. Maps where there is no exit, you must survive for as long as possible. I guess this irritates me because I know I won't beat any of you guys, so I don't have a target. My usual target is to finish, however fast it is - but on survival, I lose my target. I hate it. Irrationally, perhaps.

/edit: removed out-of-date list

Your turn.

Minimalism.
RULES: You're only allowed to use up to 10 dots of objects in the loading time. Scores out of maybe 100. This is on enjoyment of map mostly, and disregards how many objects there was. #68461 13 2005-05-22T11:22:16Z sweep
Alright, some may say I'm wasting space adding another thread for the same argument, but I believe this point deserves it's own space.

Whenever someone tells everyone "don't rate" on a map this pisses me off. You know what I do? I play the map. And I rate it. Honestly. Let me go through a few maps that say "don't rate" in the description and then i'll tell you why I bloody well should rate them however I would like to!

Checkpoints by Nevermore.
This is map is very useful. He asked for no ratings, but in my opinion that makes no sense. I rated it based on how good it was. I thought it was extremely helpful (at the time of course, now the new ned has gridding it's relatively pointless, but still) and as it was helpful to that degree it got a 5. Just because a map sets out to do something different from most maps doesn't mean it'll be rated using the same merit system as others.

The Fall of Anakin by astheoceansblue.
This is a very similar example. Someone believing that because a map is different it will get rated badly. Well, people rate maps on what they set out to do. This is good N art - I gave it a 5. Please don't ask us not to rate something in cases like this. We will rate how good we think it is. There's a reason NUMA has a ratings system!

Tri Table by Maximo.
Here we go, a very different example. Not only that, but it proves that in my opinion not even the great Maximo is exempt. Here he gives the reason that he didn't put enough effort in and so it shouldn't be rated... what a load of utter rubbish! Likewise, when people think or know they've made an awful map and they ask you not to rate it... that's beside the point! If you're going to post something on NUMA put your effort into it, make it worthwhile! If you haven't put in enough effort, put in more! You can't ask people not to rate a map because it's rubbish! That's their choice! You're liable for posting a map that might get a bad rating, it's your fault - either live with the vote, put in more effort or just don't post. As it happens, this is possibly a bad example as it's a pretty good map (unsurprisingly for Maximo) but the point still stands.

Jump N Run by BuzZzty.
Ah, this is the map that started the argument in the first place. Well, as I said in the comments, if it's a bad map either try harder, don't post or just live with the rating you get. I understand Sendy's frustrations when he/she says that asking for votes just gets you more... well, that's because people like me just get pissed off by people saying stuff like that on a site built purposely to rate maps. If you want to share your maps without them being voted, it's possible. Try it.

Non-tower Jump by Pixleman.
Once again, a case of someone asking not to rate because their map is a little different. Voters on NUMA try to vote on the merits of the map in what it was trying to set out to do (well, the majority of us do) so you have to trust us to vote for what is right. If it's a good effect, it will be rated high. A bad effect, rated low. If you think it's a bad effect, don't post it, improve it or live with the rating you get.


On top of this, who cares if you get a low rating? That map will probably not be seen for a long time because of this, but as it's a 'bad map' it wouldn't matter. Alright, your overall rating will suffer - but that's your fault. You get rated on maps you make. And to be honest, I don't care about my overall rating. The only time you should ever ask for people not to rate is if you didn't make it. And if you didn't make it, you probably shouldn't be posting it anyway.

So PLEASE, people, if you post a bad map don't ask us not to vote. It's your fault if it gets a low rating.

So PLEASE, people, if you make a map that's a little different trust us to vote it on it's true merits. We're not stupid you know, well, most of us aren't.

So PLEASE, people, don't care so much about ratings anyway. Live with your lesser appreciated maps. MOVE ON WITH YOUR LIFE...

So, PLEASE, people, if you REALLY don't want it rated, you can still share it with your friends without NUMA - there's a thing called notepad, use it!

Another point: it wasn't long ago that someone posted a map and asked people not to vote so they could still edit it... well, this was because they could post the fastest times in the level description. Don't be stupid: the comments form can be used for that.

Stick a fork in me, I am done.

#71431 4 2005-06-01T08:28:57Z sweep
Quote: Ryuk, 2005-06-01T05:43:39Z
Can you get addicted to a 2D game?

I have no problem with anything you said, apart from this ^^^^.

It shows a very closed mind to believe games are only addictive if the graphics are 3d... really, that's one of the most irrelavent aspects of gameplay you'll find. I could trawl off a list of many 2d games you could get addicted to, that many people did get addicted to before the years of several million bit graphics and flashy lights and stuff.

Let's take, as an example, the best football game ever, without a shadow of a doubt... Sensible World of Soccer. It's gameplay was far better than any football game anyone can muster these days. FIFA - fun, yes. Not the same though. Pro Ev - better than FIFA, yes. Not the same as SENSI though.

What is particularly interesting about Sensible World of Soccer, as you'll find if you read the description, is that the game lost it's appeal entirely when it 'succumbed' to the 3d graphics fad brought about by it's lesser cousin FIFA. As the description says, the 3d version was 'a dismal end to the famous series'. It was a sad sight to see.

Alright, I lied. Maybe SENSI isn't clearly the best football game ever... it ties with... no, not FIFA... no, not Pro Ev... but Championship Manager, the definitive football management game without a doubt. In past years the creators of the game have split, causing the new Championship Managers to be awful (it split into two games... one got to keep the name, the other got to keep the 'engine'... the engine one was far superior!).

Still though, the classic championship managers had something about them that people found hard to grasp... there were no graphics! Well, there were MENUS and stuff but not graphics of things moving. You found out what was happening by text. In the past few years they have updated it a bit, making it so you can see the pitch... however, each player is a dot in a very basic view of what is happening (it works though). So, before this game had ANY graphics whatsoever it was addictive... and they made the right choice to add very minimal graphics later...

I rest my case.

#3278 1 2005-06-11T20:21:26Z sweep
Right, let's say (hypothetically) that we all agreed that it was reasonable to have a maximum of two maps per page.

The current options too stop people posting more are:
1) Ask them politely not to in the comments
2) Put a warning in the NUMA system
3) Simply block submission of maps when the user has two on the page already

I am here with another suggestion. How about they can submit as many maps as they want, but they queue up? Then, once they have two on a page (or whatever we agree on), they have to wait for a new page then the map in their queue that's been waiting the longest gets submitted.

Possible problems:
1) They submit hundreds of maps in one crazy map-submitting bout and we're forced to enjoy their work for months
2) Arachnid can't implement such a system

Possible solutions:
1) a) Make it so the queue becomes full eventually at a certain number where no more can be submitted
1) Put a warning in the NUMA system
1) c) If they haven't logged onto NUMA, their maps aren't automatically submitted
2) He can ask me for help, as it would certainly be possible and I know people who would think it's a doddle. Of course, Arachnid probably would be able to do it on his own... but still.

What do you think?

This was the brief given at the start of the contest:

In the modern world, humans who skate have skateparks to show off in.

In the modern world of N, N is seriously lacking in such a thing.

And so, I bestow upon you such a challenge. You must design a level, not for the purpose of completion, but for the purpose of showing off N's tricks. Basically a skatepark, except for N. Things like bounceblocks to show his gargantuan jumps on, and thwumps positioned so N can use them catapult himself. Anything that shows off what N can do. You should also be aware that there may be things that I can't do but you can - always provide a demo with your level. If you don't, I may not discover cool stuff that you can do in it.

The rules:
You can have as many objects as you want.
Thwumps should only be used in a level as a tool to help N to cool stuff, and not to kill N. If it is possible for them to do so, it isn't a problem, but they should only be there if they can be used to do tricks.
No exits.
The thwump thing also goes for all other enemies - if it looks cool, it's good.
Final date for entry: not yet set. Will be once I get an idea of how things are turning out.
Maximum amount of entries: do as many as you want. As long as you've spent (a bit of) time on it.

The point scheme:
Appearance - 5 points
Loading time/lag (the less there is, the higher the points) - 5 points
Ease of use (if really cool tricks are easier to do it's a huge bonus) - 10 points
Fun factor (how fun is it to play?) - 20 points
Quality & Quantity of cool stuff N can do on the map - 30 points
Ninja rating (how would I rate this map on NUMA if I didn't know it was linked to this competition?) - 5 points
Originality (pretty self explanatory) - 15 points
Overall thoughts on map - 10 points
TOTAL - 100 points.
-------------------------
Judges:
Me
Eldrial/robot judge
The Daily Llama/robot judge
Jeffkillian
Maximo (backup)
tktktk (emergency backup judge)
-------------------------

#83697 17 2005-07-15T16:50:43Z sweep
Actually, I've changed my mind - as of now, judges can enter. But they don't get to rate their own map. The net effect of this is that they get one less judge giving them points and therefore less points. I've also decided there's a deadline for judges to apply of next Wednesday. I'll decide the judges after that. Right... onto the rating.


Maximo - Speed Park

Appearance
Simple, mostly tiles. I sort of felt the pipey bit in the bottom left ruined it, as it looks pretty amatuerish, especially for a Maximo map. - 3 points

Loading time/lag
There is none, well, virtually none - 5 points

Ease of use
Pretty easy to get a good flow going. To do the impressive jumps that can be done with this map takes more advanced skills - 7 points

Fun factor
Once you figure out how to do the huge jumps, this is surprisingly fun. This a great testament to minimal map making... fun can be had without enemies, or even exits - 13 points

Quality & Quantity of cool stuff N can do on the map
There's plenty of different jumps to do. They're pretty huge, as big as you're likely to get without assistance from anything other than tiles. However, the variation in tricks you can do isn't great, pretty average. Overall though, there are some damn good jumps to be had - 21 points

Ninja rating
If I saw this map on NUMA normally, I'd probably rate it at 2.5 - doesn't mean I don't think it would deserve more! As I don't like half marks, that's getting rounded up - 3 points

Originality (pretty self explanatory)
There's no particular innovation in this map, but the simplicity of it gives it a very clear sense of original style - 5 points

Overall thoughts on map

Arrogance.

It's a tricky thing.

I'm quite good at a lot of stuff. I'm very intelligent, confident, witty, entreprenuerial, musical and creative. A large chunk of people my age are complete idiots. I'm not one of them.

Is it arrogant that I believe this, or is it just confident? I know what I'm shit at. I can't swim for toffee, and for some reason I have the abilty to screw up all the time when playing most sports. Physical prowess... well, I don't really have it. I can do the high jump... pretty damn well actually, second best in my school... and I'm really bloody tall... and I'm alright at long distance running... and, I used to be really good at football and tennis. And I'm damn good at ultimate frisbee.

There you go, I went off on one again. But the thing is, all that I've just said was true. I try not to go on about it, but if someone asks me about it, why should I pretend I'm bloody good at some stuff? I, always, without a doubt come across as arrogant. But I'm not. I'm just confident. Honest. I know what I'm good at. If I'm shit at something, I'll admit it.

What's wrong with that? Perhaps it is the definition of arrogance, but even then, what's wrong with that? What isn't good is being arrogant and also ignorant. Arignorant.


So, where do you draw the line? What's arrogant? What isn't? What's wrong with being arrogant? Have you ever found you can't say something that's true without sounding arrogant?

T3h done-0rz.

Aim: To create great maps encompassing unusual use of the objects Ned provides you with. Objects should be used in ways that Mare & Raigan (creators of N) didn't intend or imagine them to be. Of course, you're allowed to use objects normally, in their intended fashion, but unusual use of objects should be highly prominent in your map.

This is NOT a bug map contest. Taking advantages of bugs within the game is allowed, but this is not a bug map contest. Also, you're not required to come up with new uses of objects. You can take heed of previous unusual uses, for example the backwards thwump effect, or the glass door effect. If you do come up with something entirely original you will gain points from it, but it is perhaps a better route to use your favourite odd objects uses in the quest to create a great map.

I figured it'd help if I gave you some examples of the types maps this contest is and isn't looking for, and why in each case.

Example of a good entry...
Pressed for Time - Lucidium.
This map encorporates backwards thwumps into a great level. This is a good entry because it uses enemies unusually and is a fully playable, enjoyable map.

Example of a bad entry...
4-bit binary adder - AlliedEnvy.
It's nice that you can use doors to create a 4-bit binary adder, but it's not a playable map in the slightest.

Example of a good entry...
Electrons - MacrossDreams
Unusual use of drones in the way they almost act as 'prison guards'. Very playable.

Example of a bad entry...
Totally Buggered - Formica (The Daily Llama)
It's a bug map. 'Nuff said.

Example of a good entry...
Compartment - Lucidium.
Well, as you've probably caught onto by now, there are two boxes to tick - unusual use of objects and playability. This one has both. The drones are used unusually in two ways... firstly, they're set still. This isn't that unusual, but isn't how M&R originally intended. Secondly, and most importantly, they're placed so they only have one clear line of view, which has rarely been seen before in this context.

RULES
- No DDAs
- No maps submitted to NUMA before the 10th of September
- Closing date for entries - 22nd of October (No more entries are allowed)
- All submitted maps should be submitted to NUMA and linked to in this thread
- No silly business
- No editing your map after it has been judged by any judge
- No more than four entries each
- No withdrawing a map that has already been partially or fully judged
- If a judge submits a map then instead of them judging it our backup judge Maximo will

Scoring of maps:
Map Quality - out of 50.
This is simply a score out of 50 points based on how good the judges think the map is, irrelevant of how it uses objects.
Object Use - out of 50.
This is a score out of 50 points based on the use of objects within the map. These 50 points should be given considering the following factors:
- the prominence of unusual object use in the map
- the importance of this unusual object use in the map
- the originality of the unusual object use in the map
- how seamlessly the unususal object use fits in the map
- generally how well the unusual used objects work within the map.
Total - out of 100.

There will be three judgings of each map, making a total out of 300.

Judges should judge the maps in order of which they were submitted.

A date for the judging to be finished has been pencilled in for the 10th of November.

#99284 7 2005-09-10T22:03:31Z sweep
Brickman, Getting Up

Map Quality
Really quite fun. Making the jumps was _very_ satisfying, and this gave it a real replay factor even after you'd completed it several times over. Asthesically it isn't the most pleasing, unfortunately, and there are a few little things that irritate me a little... like, when you're coming back down again you fall right into the path of the thwump... it's a shame really. And sometimes the launchpads just throw you back down at the ground, to get crunched on the edge of the thwump or something... maybe it'd be better, both asthesically and functionally, to just have mines instead of the launchpads lining the walls. But, at the end of the day, this is a really simple, enjoyable and exciting map all rolled into one. 37 points.

Object Use
The unusual object use is top notch here. It looks good (unlike other parts of the map... which is a little odd, but still) and it is very prominent within the map. Infact, the whole map is based around it. The use of it provides very exciting gameplay. It isn't really that original, and whilst it is visually seamless sometimes it can be a bit fiddly to negotiate. However, the map is wholly based around it, and it works really well. 39 points.

Total: 76 points.

#4437 1 2005-09-17T12:56:22Z sweep
Yesterday I was playing around with a keep rocket alive map for the "Imagination" contest when I came up with an idea... what if you completely try to eliminate N from the equation? Of course, you still have to control N, but it's not him you have to protect, it's JUST the rocket. Like a KRA map, except you're not controlling N in essence, you're controlling the rocket. It's hard to explain, but... well, I decided to make it. I soon decided it was very hard to make. I was picturing a simple gaming type console interface. Space in the middle for rocket, four "stations" on the outside, each station with three teleporters directing to each of the other stations. If you were at the station at the top, the rocket would go towards it. Station at the left, the rocket would go towards it. Etc.

I soon discovered it was very hard to make teleporters and stuff. I ended up making a "pipes" system instead, that doesn't look terribly great but satisfies the job. After many hours of working on this, the final step was to add the rocket.

Attached is the level. The rocket is very hard to control. Anyone that could supply a demo of it going the whole way round... well, I'd be impressed. This map isn't polished off, and it doesn't work... but I love the concept. Originally, in my mind, there could have been an obstacle course for the rocket to avoid, but as going round in circles is already VERY hard, I figured and obstacle course might be asking a little much.

But I love the concept. Maybe if there was someone really talented with teleporters they could make this really work.

But anyway, have a look at the level. Feel free to play around with it, do whatever you want. Make sure you credit me if you do anything on NUMA with idea... and, well, have fun.

#103010 51 2005-09-23T16:12:27Z sweep
Glenno14, Maskomitor

Map Quality
The first thing that I noticed when playing this map is naturally the first room. I find the placement of the rocket odd, because there is no incentive to take that harder route out instead of just taking the easy way out via the thwump. Odd. Anyway, the map has quite a freeform feel to it, letting you choose your route, even choose your exit. The majority of it is undeniably very easy, but it is fun enough to play, if not a tad boring after a while. The only bit that really got my excited was the rocket in the top right, which was a challenge to get past. The laser drone in the bottom left, however, serves no real purpose as you can just avoid the right wall.
Overall, this map is nice enough to play, but it doesn't give the impression of being well-thought out or polished. 23 points.

Object Use
There is plenty of UOU (unusual object use) in this map, but there's a sense that if you removed the UOU then the map would be pretty much the same. Some of the UOU, like the laser drone for example, seems out of place and just there for the sake of it. There's nothing particularly original here, and it doesn't seem very well thought out. 9 points.

Total: 32 points.

Ouch. Sorry Glenno.

Lucidium, X-rays

Map Quality
This is a very unusual map. There's a lingering sense of no matter what you do, you have NO control over what's going to happen. This is good and bad. Us N fanatics have got used to the way N is one of those games where if you go into a room, you know exactly what is going to happen. This rocket will be launched at you. This rocket will chase you. But here, this seems almost like the laser drones are beaming out almost entirely at random. On a harder map, this would have been a huge, frustrating problem. Here, it's not so much frustrating as odd. I do enjoy the predictability, but there was a sense that when I completed it it happened not because of my fantastic, agile, skillful movement throughout the level but because for no apparent reason the laser drones just didn't pick up on me.
All this said, it is a stylish level with an exciting sense of unpredictability. I like it, I really do, but the unpredictability hinders it as much as it helps. 33 points.

Object Use
UOU is at the very core of this map. The laser drones are used like I've certainly never seen them before and without them this map would be nothing. It give it a real sense of style, fits in reasonably seamlessly but is a tad too unpredictable. 42 points.

Total: 75 points.

Do you have ANY idea how many maps are submitted? Without mods, that could never happen. With mods, it'd be far too inconsistent.

Anyway, me, Lucidium and Nevermore were formulating a plan on the IRC, with assistance of Blazeraid last night. It's possibly worth pointing out that me Lucidium and NM are the three people who have rated more maps than anyone else on NUMA (although those two are in a different league altogether from me) so we spend plenty of time on NUMA, and we know it pretty well.

Basically, there should be something called The Training Grounds. From the date you post your first map on NUMA, you have to spend 15 days in the training grounds. Basically, you can't vote for other people's maps, and your maps are posted in a seperate section (which, if you haven't realised yet, is called the training grounds (what a revelation!)). Within the TG, votes would be tied with comments, meaning we would have to give constructive critisism, unless they're actually quite good, when it would be compliments, of course.

This would allow not only new people to get given advise more often, but as they couldn't vote for 15 days it would hinder both less accurate ratings and multiple accounting, as most cheats don't have the patience to wait that long. Also, as some of the rubbish maps are just people who lose interest soon after trying to make a map quickly, this would deplete the natural amount of crap on NUMA.



So... any thoughts?

#105254 107 2005-10-03T17:13:37Z sweep
This is only slightly related, but I got in a bit of trouble once to do with... well, troubling a person with OCD. I never met them, and it was one big accident... but, well...

You know those online Flash puzzles you tend to get? Well, I had a bright idea. Why not make one that is reaaaaally confusing and obscure, pretends the solution is simple and yet doesn't actually have a solution?
I created The Code. For the record, there is no way to complete it. There is no code. A lot of people ended up decompiling it to find out the answers, and some people tried all sorts of ancient code to see if they could figure it out.

Fine, right? Yes. Until, unbenownst, one day whilst I'm at school, someone with OCD logs onto my website and follows the link to The Code. This guy spends hours and hours attempting to complete The Code. After 12 hours or so of frustration, he visits my Madness Temple forums to ask for the solution. We tell him to look carefully in the FAQ - hidden in the site FAQ is the question "What is the code?" The answer is, truthfully, "there is no code". We don't hear from the person with OCD again. Done and dusted, right?

Think again.

2 days later I recieve a rather pissed off email. Apparently he read the answer in the FAQ, assumed we were taking the piss and that there was an answer. He spent much of his next two days trying to complete it. Then, at the end of it all, he discovered he could decompile it all. He downloaded Flash so he could read this file. He did everything. He discovered there was no code.

Cue really, really pissed off email. I explained how sorry I was, on how it really wasn't meant to happen, and how the FAQ was meant to be taken seriously... well, I never got an answer back. Do I feel guilty? No. It wasn't my fault. The internet must have been a death trap for people like him

Actually, maybe I have a tinge of guilt. But still. What was I supposed to do?

#4610 1 2005-10-04T17:15:28Z sweep
This is the third time I'm writing the introduction for this topic. TWICE the window with the introduction has closed down, and every time it has got shorter and shorter. It was originally bloody long. Anyway, I'm gonna make this quick before someone shuts down my computer just before I press submit:

This thread is what it says on the tin - my NUMA commentary, basically NUMA in tiny bitesized chunks. I'll give my opinions on what's going on, and tell you about the good, the bad, and the ugly. Basically, it'll be a summary of what's going on at NUMA. Perfect if you only want to see a few maps, and also great for starting off conversation based on NUMA. Feel free to add your opinions, or anything you think I may have missed out. I won't be updating this every day, and I won't be looking at every map, so join in: write your own accounts. Go for it.

4th October
Weather: N00b heavy as usual, but quite a lot of great maps considering the time of year.
Firstly, I'll start off with my favourite map from the day.
Rose is N Art at it's best - simple and effective. I also like the way it's a rose made of mines, as that's perhaps symbolic. Sure, they were chosen because they're red, but I like the accidental hidden message nonetheless. It's gone in my favourites.
Random Shapes was another high quality map. Perhaps not perfect, but it showcases BenMiff's growing style and map-making talent.
The worst map of the day, in my opinion, is the abomination that is Simple Challenge? Putting shame to the good simple challenge name, this is simply awful. Needless overuse of enemies: check. Unoriginal use of enemies: check. Tileset that's been given no thought whatsoever: check. Load of bollocks: er, check.
Whilst My little Tribute to formica is a little awkward at times, and clusters enemies, it isn't too bad. But this isn't why I'm highlighting this map: look at the bottom of the page. Yes, tremble and fear, for local little bastard craftymerchant is back on NUMA. As many of you know, he's evading the ban under the name of craftymerchantR. How idiotically crafty of him. Anyhoo, I thought I'd point out that he's already trying to cause trouble again with a needless "boo" comment. Sure, it isn't that exciting, but he needs to be watched with an eager eye.
I can't help but feel Jumping Up The Schrappnel is needlessly overrated. It's a nice tileset, sure, and an easy map is always nice, but... well, you can bypass half the map by just jumping up the left wall. Doesn't that defeat the point completely? It just feels a tad unexciting and not very well made. Don't get me wrong: I am enjoying Macaddict's maps, but this is overrated. It is now 4/5 after I rated it, but it was 4.5/5. Overrated. 'Nuff said.
To finish with, Heart Broken is a rather nice map.

DISCLAIMER: any offence caused is only because I want to make you cry

(I'm not sure how well this thread will work, we'll have to see if people are interested)

#105872 3 2005-10-06T07:58:48Z sweep
Simple solution: Only the middle 5/6 ratings count towards the average rating.

EG...

For 2, 2, 2.5, 2.5 and 5 all votes are counted.
For 1.5, 2, 2, 2.5, 2.5 and 6 all votes are counted.
For 0, 1.5, 2, 2, 2.5, 2.5 and 3 only votes in bold are counted.
For 0, 1.5, 1.5, 2, 2, 2.5, 2.5 and 3 only votes in bold are counted.
For 0, 0, 0, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4.5, 4.5, 4.5, 4.5, 4.5, 5, and 5 only votes in bold are counted.

For odd numbers of ratings, the middle 5 votes are counted. For even numbers of ratings, the middle six. This will eliminate sniping and poor voting in general.

I've suggested this before, but not in such a comprehensive form. What do you think?

#105982 13 2005-10-06T18:59:35Z sweep
6th October (includes maps from day before too)
Weather: It has to be said, the n00b hurricane of the past few weeks seems to have cleared up. The past two days have been pretty good... but there are still plenty of n00bish maps and moments around good ol' NUMA.
Here we go...
The Magnetic Fields is a great ambassador for simplicity everywhere. Such a simple concept, and it works really nicely, and it feels really polished.
Aju proved his growing map talent with the lovely looking, lovely playing Delerious. The asymetric tileset works great with N moving about on it. Excellent work.
Meanwhile, the award for most suspiciously overrated goes to the plain awful Rat Race. God knows how this, for a start, was given a vote of 5 from someone. Furthermore, God knows how after 6 votes this map remains on 3 ninjas. This, quite frankly, is taking the piss. It's an awful map.
Of course, maybe Rat Race wouldn't have been given this award if it wasn't for
Speed Is The Key not reaching the five votes needed to reveal its average rating. How did Speed Is The Key get a 4.5 from wellsj? I'd like to find out, but until now I'm just going to go over to a corner and cry.
It is always notable when tktktk returns with another of his fantastic Simple Challenge series. #16 is nothing more than you'd expect from what has gone before.
Also notable is the return of the irreplaceable Sendy to the map-making fray. Dave Cut The Record Down To The Bone is a vintage Sendy piece of work.
The worst description of the past 24 hours has to be given to the odd beach+mine collaboration of Mine jumping in water. The title sounds slightly Japanese and the description lives up to it - poor grammar, and frankly it is just a bit odd.
Meanwhile, somewhere else on Earth, Have A Slope was simply just quite fun. It was unexpected, sure, and after a while this loses its replay value, but it's loveably simple and fun. It doesn't look great, but it doesn't matter! It is also completely unoriginal, but I don't care.
Something is not only a crap name for a DDA, but a crap DDA.
However, Ironmuffins is a great name for a DDA, and a great DDA. Really excellent work. Enjoy the show.


That's me done.

Also: come on people! For this thread to work we need contributions. It doesn't matter how small they are. If you see something on NUMA that you really like, or really hate, just post here saying so. Want to point out anything? Here's the place.

You missed it. Read my posts more thoroughly!

Expert and elite members may vote on any maps at all, but novice members may only vote and comment on novice maps. The only perk to being elite is that your map and name shows up in gold when you submit or comment. So elite is just a thing to aim for and shows people on NUMA which map-makers have made a whole lot of great maps.

Also, the average rating 3 isn't very elite at all, now is it? 3 is average. Elite members are members whose maps are quite plentiful and consistently above average (3.5 or higher). Experts are members whose maps are fairly numerous and at least moderately good (2.5 or higher).

Novices are members whose maps are few or whose maps are consistently below average. That means a set of seven 4-rated maps is still novice--this member needs to contribute more to NUMA before he can become an expert. Also, a set of eighty 1-rated maps is still novice--this member needs to improve his map-making skills before he can become expert.

Again, the primary success of this system is that it relies on both map-making consistency and map-making skill.

Ha! You missed it! Read my post more thoroughly.

By lowering it to 3 I did not mean the average rating they needed, but the amount of votes and elite map would need to show up it's rating.

#109982 112 2005-10-23T15:13:55Z sweep
Hellheart, Bouncy Bouncy!

Map Quality
This is a really odd map... parts of it play like a DDA and it looks a lot like many DDAs do too (that isn't a compliment). It doesn't look like it has anything really holding it together, it doesn't look like it was made with a plan in mind. It feels like it was made up as Hellheart went along. I dunno, it's just not right. It doesn't look particularly nice, and whilst there are a few nice parts... well, it's just really messy. To be honest, I don't really understand the whole exit thing, the gold placement is a bit odd at times and the enemy placement is a bit odd. When I first played this when it was originally submitted, I only played the beginning section - which on it's own is promising. But overall this map is just plain messy. 23 points.

Object Use
Ok, there is plenty of unusual object use here. It is used quite nicely at some points, and quite pointlessly at others. The problem is, I can't help but feel the reason why this map feels messy is purely down to the UOU. It fails to blend in, and doesn't add enough to map to warrant its inclusion. 13 points.

Total: 36 points.


Hellheart, Dim-N-Tia

Map Quality
I think Coldcut summed this up rather well. His words were "doesnt quite make sense but i think your on to something" and my opinion isn't too far off. I'm rather fond of this little map. The idea is great. In parts, it works like a charm. Unfortunately #1: it's a tad confusing. Unfortunately #2: it's far to easy to complete the way it isn't supposed to be completely. I stumbled upon the exit in a chronic mass of confusion. I'd managed to accidentally skip half the route... not on purpose, it just happened. This is a shame. I love the way the map works, I love the idea behind it, but it is quite simple broken. 32 points.

Object Use
This map is all about the UOU. And it is used in a rather innovative manner, and although it looks messy it does kinda fit in. It makes the map charming and exciting. Shame it proved too difficult for Hellheart to make the map watertight. 25 points.

Total: 57 points.


Brickman, Hunter

Map Quality
It looks good and it plays quite well. It is, on the other hand, too hard for the likes of me. I didn't have enough patience to get far on this, and my interest would have died out if it weren't for the demo there for me to watch. I can appreciate that this is a good map, but the truth it I never had the chance to enjoy it. Also, someone with more patience than me could easily cheat the whole map - the rocket doesn't need to follow you the whole way round, you just need to draw it out at the end THEN make it follow you back in.
Meh. 34 points.

Object Use
Well, it's all about the UOU. What can I say? The UOU blends in well, is nearly watertight (with exception of the end) and plays quite well. It isn't original, of course, but that doesn't matter. 38 points.

Total: 72 points.
#110002 114 2005-10-23T18:50:02Z sweep
Hellheart, Flaccid

Map Quality
This map can compare directly to my map The Mooney Suzuki. The Mooney Suzuki is a similar thwump-based map. The great thing about the Mooney Suzuki was that your options were wide open - there were so many routes you could take, it really tested your ingenuity and no routes were immediately obvious. However, some people also found themselves unexcited by it, and that it was a bit pointlessly cryptic... and just lacked that "something". Needless to say, I think Flaccid is a better map. However, I feel it shares the same problems, as well as the same positive features. 36 points.

Object Use
This map is entirely based around the UOU, which looks the part but throws up a few minor problems. It has been done before... not many times quite as well as this... 37 points.

Total: 73 points.


Nevermore, Shot Down

Map Quality
This map suffers from FUOU syndome. Faulty unusual object use syndrome. The map looks the part, and would play the part, if not ultimately for the failings of the trapdoor/launch pad system; which is too hard, cryptic and especially over-temperamental. The sections without the trapdoor/launchpad system are reasonably nice, but nothing to get overly excited about. Mr. Nevermore states that the trapdoor/launchpad "challenge" is part of the fun - but I don't have the patience, nor the skill, to see the fun(ny) side. 33 points.

Object Use
Potentially very good. Also reasonably original. But it's too hard to surpass, and too temperamental. 14 points.

Total: 47 points.
#110033 116 2005-10-23T20:37:26Z sweep
I'm sorry man. I really didn't want to give you a poor score.

Those doors just weren't very fun.

MOLONEY, I Like Datarock

Map Quality
It's a rather charming, simple little map. Quite playable, and although it isn't brilliant and really exciting, there's something likeable about it. It's minimalistic, and looks good as a result. It's enjoyable to play, but admittedly doesn't have too much replay factor. 33 points.

Object Use
The object use of the thwump isn't that unusual, but it is a bit different. The whole map revolves around walljumping of it and getting out of areas before it locks you in... nothing special, but hey, it works. 22 points.

Total: 55 points.


Euphoria, Ducking Under

Map Quality
Clever idea, and it the map looks quite nice, is designed well, and poses a good but realistic challenge. But we have one problem. There is a lot of waiting involved. When you're on a launchpad, it takes the excitement out just waiting for your moment. And also, coming off the launchpad is slow and hard to perfect... but hey, 'tis still rather nice. 35 points.

Object Use
Only one problem - the waiting and the coming off the launchpad. The idea itself is pretty faultless, and it all fits into the map rather nicely. 32 points.

Total: 67 points.


Euphoria, Industrial Age

Map Quality
Nice idea, implemented in a simple and affective way. Possibly a bit hard to master getting the switches without frame, but this works really well. The seeker drone adds a much needed dimension to the map. 38 points.

Object Use
Implemented in a simple, affective system. A little hard to get at the switches, but original, different and fun nonetheless. 37 points.

Total: 75 points.


Euphoria, Piano Keys

Map Quality
Simple, stylish... adds a new element to N, and whilst at first it feels almost like there is no skill to it, there certainly is. In my opinion the current 3/5 ninja score it has is a little harsh, as I think it's a charming map that people maybe didn't have the patience to figure out properly. It isn't that hard, it's even quite fun! 37 points.

Object Use
Piano keys describes the UOU in this perfectly. It's almost like there's a new enemy in the game. It's original, it's well implemented, and it adds a whole new dimension to the gameplay. It's a tad unpredictable at times, but I don't think it matters. 40 points.

Total: 77 points.

I shall prove that you can't walk any given distance.

Take a distance. 1 meter. Walk half of that. 0.5 meters. Walk a half of the distance you are yet to travel. 0.25 meters. You have now travelled 0.75 meters. Walk a half of the distance you are yet to travel. 0.125 meters. You have now travelled 0.875 meters. Repeat ad infinitum; you will never, ever travel the full meter. #110391 123 2005-10-25T13:25:15Z sweep
Brickman, Tight Squeeze

Map Quality
Well, to put it simply, it has been done before, just not in this way. This is simply a more inventive version of "tight squeeze tile" theme maps that have gone before. The first time I played for this map I really enjoyed it, but on repeat plays it shows up as a tad frustrating and less playable. Nonethless, a good map. 33 points.

Object Use
It's all about the tight squeeze. Been done before, although perhaps not in all these forms. There is something frustrating about this format though... getting stuck in the middle is just really irritating. 31 points.

Total: 64 points.


SOLARION, The Rage of Innocence

Map Quality
It's just not good at all. The thwumps are tedious and repetitive. The strange drone in doors part is plain stupid, when the drones could have just been NaN'd for a far more affective, er, effect. The laser drone section is better, if not a bit unoriginal. Then you enter the jumppad section, an idea that has been tried unsuccessfully far too often - there's just too much luck to it. And finally... well, my favourite room! At last something interesting and playable! The bounce blocks and jumppads are a good combo. You get to the end of the room and breath a sigh of relief. Then you realise you have to do everything you've just done, but backwards. Stuff it: this is the moment when I closed down N. 13 points.

Object Use
UOU #1 - drones in doors. Odd, unaffective and there are far better alternatives, I'm afraid. UOU #2 - bounceblocks and jump pads. Better this time. But nothing special. 20 points.

Total: 33 points.


Hellheart, Another Doomsday Machine

Map Quality
A goodish idea overdone. It doesn't look to good - but this isn't really too much of a problem. The whole idea is just overdone and not forgiving enough. I can't complete the very begining section. Yes, no matter what I try, I can't get to the section with the backwards thwumps. Thing is, other parts of the map are more forgiving and therefore more enjoyable - just like in everyday life, it's minority that ruins it for everyone. 18 points.

Object Use
Good use of UOU. Not perfect though, and not stunningly original. 33 points.

Total: 51 points.

Macaddict, Thwump Rampage 1

Map Quality
This map is not too far removed from "Another Doomsday Machine". It looks tidier, and if far easier. But there's something inneffably imperfect and unpolished about it all. It is quite fun to play, but some parts are a bit unexciting. Nonetheless, general a nice map. 33 points.

Object Use
Riding thwumps - simple + affective. It works. Not too original, and nothing special. 33 points.

Total: 66 points.


rrrobyp, Strange Rocket Path

Map Quality
This is a good map that I feel almost tries too hard to fit in with the contest guidelines... the kra theme works well, although I find it odd that it is rather obselete at the start of the map. I've come to expect KRA maps to be more along the lines of keeping the rocket alive for the entirety of your run. But hey, this is a minor quibble. I love the trapdoor system, where you have to spring just the right amount, but it can be a bit frustrating when you overshoot - it is really easy to do accidentally. Overall, the map is rather nice, although certainly not what rrrobyp is capable of. 34 points.

Object Use
Quite a few instances of UOU in this map - all well implemented, though not entirely faultless and not incredibly original. 35 points.

Total: 69 points.


Korbachev, Run, Thwump, Run!

Map Quality
Potentially brilliant - merely pretty good. It's exhilarating and exciting. Some parts aren't completely smooth in transition though, the bottom room is a let down and overall it doesn't look particularly great. Nonetheless: it is undeniably fun. 39 points.

Object Use
Works well. Not particularly original. Makes the map exciting. 'Nuff said. 39 points.

Total: 78 points.


BenMiff, Black Escort

Map Quality
This map is an exploration of the classic "prisoner" format. There have undoubtably been better prisoner maps, but this isn't bad at all. It plays quite well, with some sections more successful than others. It's a good, solid map. I won't be playing it again though. 37 points.

Object Use
Affective. Not that original. 35 points.

Total: 72 points.


Lucidium, Crash Into Me

Map Quality
It was only a matter of time. Sooner or later Lucidium was going to come up with an entry of this calibre sooner or later. It looks beautifully polished, and plays somewhat unusually, but still very well. The gold is placed with thought and care. Perhaps it's a little confusing for someone who doesn't know where the gold is - maybe half tiles could have worked better there? Also, it can be a bit frustrating, repeatedly hitting the wall but sometimes with little luck. But still - it's original, different and it plays well. 43 points.

Object Use
It has been done before, though not often, and not in this form. It works quite well - although logistically maybe half tiles just to show where the switches are would help next time. It can be a bit frustrating (liking hitting your head against a brick wall.... *ahem*) but as tktktk says, it certainly is "well realised". 39 points.

Total: 82 points.


Barabajagal, One Flew Over the Cukoo's Nest

Map Quality
A really nice, well built, level. It's the kind of map that leaves your options wide open. It's a shame that you can hop right up the wall though, and perhaps the level is slightly too simple, and needs a few more drones, or instead there could be a spattering of rocket launchers. Still, a really nice level. 42 points.

Object Use
The use of UOU isn't too particular. It's just generally riding/using thwumps in a variety of ways. You can complete the map without using any of these techniques... which isn't good, as although UOU is a feature of the map, it isn't definitely at the forfront. The UOU does add plenty of gameplay to the map though - and the freedom of the level caused by it is a bit different. 34 points.

Total: 76 points.

Barabajal, Peruvian Backgammon

Map Quality
It's a really nice combination of backwards thwumps and riding thwumps. It looks great and for the most part, it plays great. My only real problem with this map is the way that drones can get in your way and you can't really do anything about it. Perhaps it is also a tad repetitive, as it is the same thing over and over again. But it is a well oiled, near perfect concept - and to top it off, it does play rather well. 40 points.

Object Use
A combination of two tried and tested ideas. What can I say? It works really well. 42 points.

Total: 82 points.



*collapses in a sweaty heap of judgingly mess*

#111619 134 2005-10-31T13:26:50Z sweep
Euphoria, Virtual Voyage

Map Quality
This map looks great. It sets a realistic challenge, and is easy enough to play and fun enough too. It has been well thought out, with the sloping floor making up for the pillars that can be hard to grip on when already falling. The gausses can be a bit annoying, and perhaps a generally less irritating enemy would have done better in their place. Nonetheless, this is a fun and original map that has been carried out with hard to fault conviction. 39 points.

Object Use
The teleporter system is well implemented and running through the whole of this map. One does wonder, however, whether it could have been more reliable if implemented slightly differently; it isn't the most reliable of systems. 35 points.

Total: 74 points.


Mithril Silver, Golden Stars

Map Quality
I've never been a fan of such drone-pattern-heavy maps. The flow feels very much dictated by drones which are frustratingly slower than you, and... well, drone-heavy maps also tend to succumb to awful lag. This one doesn't lag very much at all on my computer, though. I've also always felt a bit bored when there's not an exit to get to - going for all-gold never excites me. Sure, this is probably quite an unreasonable stance to take, but going for gold just doesn't excite me. So, well, me and this map didn't get along too well. All that said, however, it looks real pretty with the drone patterns and it plays alright, although the jump pads are overly-awkward. 27 points.

Object Use
... what's meant to be the UOU? The jump pads? The drones? I have very little idea. But the jump pads are used sort of unusually, I suppose. 6 points.

Total: 33 points.


Mithril Silver, mini challenge: tight squeeze

Map Quality
Quite simply, it's a tiny, little, easy, unusual and charming mini-map. The rocket is prone to going through the trap doors which is a problem, but overall it's a nice little map. 31 points.

Object Use
Lot's of small uses of UOU. Quite nice, but there's no real theme of the same UOU throughout. 30 points.

Total: 61 points.


Disintegrator, Drill

Map Quality
It's a really simple, well made map. It's quite easy, but fun to match up with it. Perhaps a little gold wouldn't have gone amiss, but apart from that I can't really fault this map. It's simple, small, and perfectly formed. 36 points.

Object Use
I don't think there's much UOU to be honest... I mean, the small corridor thing with drones isn't really UOU, and the gold on the exit switch... I suppose it is, but it doesn't serve too much of a purpose... 8 points.

Total: 44 points.


TornadoTK, Spontaneism

Map Quality
As Mr. Tornado says himself, it is rather sloppy. But it plays pretty well, and allows room for adventure and exploration of different routes. It feels unusual to play, probably because it damn well is, and it's very sloppy and I'd say it's pretty imperfect - but, you know, I like it. 35 points.

Object Use
A lot of UOU is embedded within this map. Some of it is harder to find... but all in all, it really is quite interesting. It suffers from the lack of a UOU theme, though, IMO. 37 points.

Total: 72 points.


Adam Dobay, Temple of Sekhmet

Map Quality
Ew! Lag! Yep, it's a real problem. Luckily, it doesn't render the map on my computer entirely unplayable, but still, it's frustrating, and the sucks the fun out right away. And there's too much waiting for drones to distinguish their laser... not too fun, I'm afraid. 23 points.

Object Use
Simple UOU, that could have been affective if it weren't for the lag it causes. Not especially original. 22 points.

Total: 45 points.

#5018 1 2005-11-03T16:55:30Z sweep
Ok. Scenario 1:
Map gets high rating. User plays map, and believes it is a lower rating in their opinion than the rating it currently is. Say, someone who doesn't like DDAs. A DDA ends up as a 5, and our someone would rate it a 3.5. This someone decides that because they would only lower the rating, they'll just not vote at all.
This is where the voting system breaks down. I don't like jumper maps as much as other maps. This doesn't mean I shouldn't vote on them. The whole point of voting is to find everyone's opinions and average them out. If you exclude people voting it lower, then you're just getting the opinions of people that really like said map. Feel guilty being responsible for a map getting rated down? Don't. It's your opinion, and the voting is there to voice your opinion.

Scenario 2:
I only have only experienced this problem once, but it irritated me nonetheless. I rated a map 4.5 instead of 5 because all _14_ rockets made it lag really badly. Then someone complained about me doing this. They said that it didn't lag on their computer. Therefore, they claimed, I shouldn't have rated it down for lag. This pissed me off. Firstly, how am I supposed to know it doesn't lag on someone elses computer? Secondly, maps should be built to cater the widest range of computers possible without hampering the gameplay/visuals too much. My computer isn't incredibly laggy, but anything in the region of _14_ rockets will definitely lag it, and that's not my fault, or my computers fault. The map is a 4.5 ninja map from my point of view, therefore. When combined with non-laggy computers, this will result in a fair score. This again links to scenario 1.

Basically: rate it on the basis of how you enjoyed it/how it played on your computer, not how anyone else enjoyed it. The rating system is there for you to voice your opinion. Use it.

/edit: also, on another note, I don't think indimidation of people who might like a map less is acceptable either. For example, here where Ben Schultz says "If anyone rates this lower than 4.5..." He might not be saying a lot, but it's seriously gonna put people off rating anything less. This skewers the voting system. Therefore it's bad news. There's nothing wrong with saying anything about snipers, as that's different, but people should feel entitled to rating a map 2, 3.5, 4, whatever. As long as it is a truthful vote based on how they enjoyed the map.

/edit edit: Another thing... if you have a map that you like that gets rated down, don't delete it because it has been rated down. If you think the map is worthy of your collection, keep it there. Ignore the rating, it's irrelevant. If you don't think the map is up to standard, then you delete it.
#112076 138 2005-11-03T17:30:48Z sweep

#113912 17 2005-11-11T20:13:28Z sweep
To respond to why I don't think the non-action categories can compete:
Puzzle - It's just... well, N isn't built for puzzles. Every now and again someone makes a brilliant puzzle, but the fact is, most puzzles aren't really puzzles. Even good puzzles are quite easily monotonous an uninspiring though - that said, there are a few that I love.
Race - too linear.
Survival - just not as satisfying. For it to be fun, you really have to be competing with someone else. In most maps, the real satisfaction is getting to the exit, but there's always the competing with others side. There's only one survival map I've ever loved, and that's Evil Bob's Fear of Crowds one... enoclophobia or something...
DDA - I'm sorry, but the novelty has worn out for me. You watch it once, you go "wow", then that's it. They've now all converged into one huge mess of the same style DDAs anyway, and I've come to realise that making a really good DDA takes less skill and more dedication. With an action map, it takes a real touch, a real eye for things to make the map great. But with a DDA, as long as you know the basic rules, you can make a great one by just spending ages on it. Don't get me wrong, it's impressive, but... meh. I just don't enjoy watching them anymore. It's oooollld news.
Test Level - Well, I don't think I need to explain why this category pales in comparison to action.


One of the other great things about action is the scope it leaves you with. There are probably so many great potential ideas for action maps that haven't been explored yet... action is king, and always will be.

Amen.

#114145 154 2005-11-12T13:43:36Z sweep
Jiggerjaw12358, Heaps of Hidden Helpers

Map Quality
First things first: this is a clever map. There's no denying it. But I would like to question whether it really plays well enough. I find the start difficult and frustrating, and this can go for some other parts too. The first time you do almost every section of this map, you really don't know what to expect. This means you die, and it tests your perserverance to continue trying the map again and again. I just didn't enjoy playing this map, simple as that. It's not big... but it is clever. 32 points.

Object Use
Clever and unusual although already explored UOU - but the gameplay suffers from it. 35 points.

Total: 67 points.


Gogiga Thingamee Hard Name To Spell Without Referring to The Original Spelling, Laser Shroom

Map Quality
It looks great. It plays great. It's brim full of enemies, yet its tiny landscape means it doesn't lag. And yet, despite its tiny landscape, there is plenty to explore. The bounceblocks and thwumps don't get in the way as much as I expected, although this is a small issue nonetheless. All in all, I really like this map. I can't find any major faults in it, and it plays like a beast. 44 points.

Object Use
Well, it's been done before, and debateably better than this. But it's still great here. If this was original, the score would be hitting the roof - but this isn't all that different from what's been done before. 40 points.

Total: 84 points.


krusch, Necropolis

Map Quality
My first impressions were not the same as my final impressions. It looks fantastic at first, but seems to suffer from a case of TBG - tileset before gameplay. The thwumps just don't fit in quite right, and it therefore doesn't play very well. Nonetheless, I continued to play this map. Boy was I surprised. Normally, I would have just dismissed this as a nice tileset with poor gameplay, but I went on to discover a really nice piece of gameplay underneath. I enjoyed completing the level. I enjoyed it quite a lot. It felt a bit like a puzzle, even though it wasn't in the slightest. Whilst the gameplay at first seems poor, its simplicity really works, despite not immeadiately grabbing you. It's a shame that most of it will given up on it far too soon. 42 points.

Object Use

#5191 1 2005-11-14T17:09:38Z sweep
Some people may remember a time on Ned where you could remove the border tiles. Well, I propose this is reinstated. With two modifications.

Firstly, the level code includes info that the border no longer exists. Just something like a b1 for a border, a b2 for no border. This could be at a convienient place in the code where it could be removed easily or could be ignored by an old version of Ned. Those of you that were around when borders could be taken off will remember that although you could remove the border tiles, the level code would not store info about the border tiles and so when someone else loaded it up the tiles would remain.

Secondly, so it's not just N falling into an abyss forever, when he crosses the bottom of the screen (where the bottom of the border is) he would automatically die. He could get flung up above the top of the screen, as long as he came back down and landed (etc. etc.) Of course, it would just be an y value to cross that would kill him, so he could be a million miles wide of the screen, but if he crossed that y value he'd die.

Basically, this would not only save us from lining the edges with mines, but would give the game many more possibilities (long range laser drones, blind jumping, MASSIVE JUMPS etc.) due to the larger space possible to inhabit, and ultimately shouldn't be too hard to code.

Any thoughts?

NOTE: Due to time restrictions, I haven't read back through what I just typed. Feel free to correct me.

#5210 1 2005-11-15T16:59:03Z sweep
Firstly, I'd like to point out that I'm not taking any credit for this idea. This was completely prompted by Nevermore coming up with it as a solution. I've just decided it deserves a thread of its own - this idea needs to be taken seriously.

The concept: well, it's simple. No more ratings. Abolish them completely.

Those of you that haven't heard this idea before will probably right now be thinking this is ridiculous - surely ratings are what makes NUMA brilliant? Competition only makes us better and better, right?

My first reaction to the idea was simple: yeah, it would solve a lot of problems, but I wondered whether I really, in my heart of hearts, would feel disheartened by the sudden lack of ratings to inflate my ego, or, equally, deflate it. But in the few hours since my original reaction, I've had time to think it through.

I think this is best to explain by looking at the history of NUMA. You know that "golden age" that so many people go on about? What brought about the fall of this "age"? The answer is obvious: ratings. Think of a problem that NUMA has, and it is very often due to or provoked by ratings. So, let's remember two things: firstly that NUMA's golden age was golden during a time without a ratings system (towards the end, yes, it did have a ratings system, but that's what brought about its fall) and secondly that NUMA is the mess it is right now mainly due to ratings.

As someone mentioned in another thread, ratings seemed like a nice enough idea at the time, but no-one took a big enough pause to really think it through. A monster was created - but it was no-ones fault.

This is what I ask: if you're completely opposed to this idea, pause for a few minutes and think. Think about whether you really need ratings, and whether you long to see the second golden age of NUMA.

Of course, ultimately, it's Arachnid's choice whether to remove ratings; but let's let him know what we think.

So?

/edit: a few minor tweaks made for accuracy
#115239 74 2005-11-15T18:05:32Z sweep
I'd like to preceed my judging with a short note.

The rating I give the maps is roughly based on what I'd give the map in the NUMA ratings system. That means a 50 is equivalent to a 5 - so, basically, I'd just like people to be prepared for lower ratings. Making small maps is hard, and as such the maps are less likely to rate well on NUMA, and therefore likewise for me. So, good luck to everyone.

Nevermore, Capcom
This is going sound ridiculous, but I actually rather like the tileset in this one. Well, I think it maximises the use of tiles rather well considering only 5 could be used. But the tileset isn't important, it's the gameplay that it's all about. Well, this map definitely suffers from the lack of objects. It doesn't feel complete. The drone usage is an interesting but slightly uneconomic use of objects - and in this contest ecocomy is really important. 3 objects for just the one small section - well, it could have been spent better otherwise. But nonetheless, this isn't bad for a first entry. 23 out of 50

47percent, The Slaughter of the Inner Child
This success and also the failure of this map is the use of the entire landscape. It's obvious really - who needs 5 tiles when you can just make the big border round the outside part of the level? Now that's what I can economic. But unfortunately, one rocket is just too small to cover such a large space effectively and to your little ninja's danger. However, the top part of the map is more interesting, and overall the map does work. Just about. But there is no question that it feels incomplete. 27 out of 50

tl, i need more space!
Well, it's impressive that this really does function as a puzzle. Unfortunately, solving the puzzle is more a case of persistance as opposed to deep thought. Just keep on jumping until you discover the ideal route - or at least, that's what I did, and it didn't take too long. It's a nice little map though, and the way the thwumps have been arranged poses an intruiging challlenge. 28 out of 50

#118043 132 2005-11-25T23:17:09Z sweep
Sucker1, Falling.
Quite nice, but it certainly looks and feels bare and incomplete. There is nice scope for PYF, and landing on the slope is an interesting challenge.
33 points.

Deadly, Jump Man.
Booooring. So incredibly simple that gameplay has been taken out of this. The only exciting thing is jumping all three drones in one go... which leaves me feeling a bit "meh". Not well thought through, not maximising the use of the objects.
19 points.

stl1234, Keep it simple & speedy.
The main problem with this map is that the tiles and the locked door are easily made redundant by the outside walls. If you don't use the outside walls, it becomes more interesting, but still feels bare and incomplete.
22 points.

Kai_Robert, Simpleandhard.
Aha! Now this is what the previous map should have been like. Beautifully constructed, really fun to play, impossible to cheat, and really exciting to try and do speed runs! Fantastic. However, it is too linear, really - but this is just a very minor problem. Excellent entry.
41 points.

Evil_Bob, Box of What Now?
This is a rather tiny little map, and it plays alright, but quite simply has no replay factor for me at all.
27 points.

astheoceansblue, something vague.
The angled tiles give this many possibilities for completion, and pose an interesting challenge. This map suffers from, like many other entries to this competition, the ability to "cheat" by using the outside walls. A nice entry, but something just doesn't add up for me.
35 points.

Ngaged, square hop.
Cool idea, reasonably well realised. However, you can scale the walls and cheat. With the allowance of tiles and objects Ngaged had left, he could have easily stopped this being possible. Also, this type of map is hardly a new concept.
30 points.

MasterJMD, Jumperfic!
Oh, come on. There's simple, and then there's this. I just find this a bit boring and annoying, to be honest.
26 points.

KLUMPEET, Simplicity.
Nice-ish to play, and good for speed runs, but to be frank I found this pretty unexciting.
31 points.

wellsj, Deep Red.
Interesting map with interesting use of both tiles and objects, but a little frustrating to play.
33 points.

wellsj, Controlled Falling.
As far as this contest goes this is one of the most original entries so far. Personally, I didn't have fun playing this map, but can appreciate the economic use of objects.
35 points.

stl1234, What 3 things...
Reasonably clever use of objects and tiles. It plays alright, but just isn't FUN enough to get high marks.
31 points.

villemance, Breaking Your Fall.
Innovative? Yes. An interesting puzzle, if not a little too trial and error for my liking. I got bored of it after a while.
34 points.

InuyashaDuelist, A Day At School.
I feel an overwhelming sense of dejavu. At least this is harder to cheat, but there is less corner jumping involved.
30 points.

Spondoogie, 5.
Good for speed runs and nothing else.
28 points.

Spondoogie, 97
Very similar concepts have been better realised in this contest. But this isn't bad, granted. Shame it's cheatable.
34 points.

Pinko, Pimpo.
W00T! SIMPLE STEALTH! Excellent. Good for speed runs, good for non-speed runs, but a tad cheatable.
37 points.

Virtual_Cyberspace, Less is More.
I really like the beginning. The rest... is a little unimaginative. It's a all a little too simple; let's not kid ourselves, less isn't usually more. Not in this case.
27 points.

I_Spy, Incompident.
Pretty fun to play... if you don't cheat. This feels more like a complete map than most entries so far. The gauss placement is a little weird though.
33 points.

Wellsj, Barracks.
The second fun & simple stealth map so far. The tile placement is a little unimaginative, but the gold placement works really well and the chaingun is an affective enemy. Nice, but all in all still feels slightly awkward and incomplete.
36 points.

Krusch, Interpol.
An affective, interesting entry. The drone system works really well. However, the type of map that depends strongly on a talent for the timing of a string of jumps isn't really my cup of tea, which is a shame.
34 points.

#112572 (forumer) 5 2005-11-30T20:18:00Z sweep
The story behind the username "Sweep" is a long and complex one.

It was just yesteryear when I was whaling in Southern Europe, albeit unsuccessfully. I set to sea with one dream - to catch the Powder Whale, a largish whale common near areas like Spain and famous for it's powder-like look. Little was I to know that my boat was riddled with rats. Four days in, I noticed my food supplies slowly starting to diminish at an unlikely rate. After another four days, I was out of food altogether, and clinging to the top of the mast to avoid the scurrious rats. It was pure hell, and the sea didn't help matters; the water became incredibly ferocious, with huge climbing tidal waves engulfing everything in sight. My life was in danger. In such peril, I decided that as I had my wi-fi laptop with me, and there was an oil rig with a wireless internet connection nearby, I'd have a quick web session. It was then that I discovered a photo-shopping community named b3ta. The site thrilled me so much that I had to register. I registered as my usual, somewhat odd internet username of dogbuttocks. However, there was already a b3ta member named dogsbollocks so they suggested I changed my name for clarity. In a fit of confusion, I spontaneously mashed my keyboard, and the result that came up was "chimneysweep". Then, when I came to these forums several months later, the registration form wouldn't accept the username "chimneysweep", so I tried "Sweep" and it worked! Several days later, I died at sea returned to England to spend my days writing music and surfing the web.

#119584 118 2005-12-01T18:23:22Z sweep
Voting rules:

1) No voting for yourself.
2) No voting more than once per category choice.
3) If you wish to decline to vote in a category you may, and if you wish to decline to vote in a category choice.
4) If I wish to decline your votes, I will tell you so. I reserve the right to do this. I will only do it with very good reason, and it's unlikely it will have to happen. I might well tell people about it on this thread, to get a second opinion.
5) Please don't tell other people what you voted for. It ruins the fun. Of course, it's your secret, tell whoever you wish to, or hint at it, whatever, but it does ruin the fun; try to avoid it.
6) Don't throw pointed objects, you could have someone's eye out.

Vote counting system:

The choices are each worth thus:
1st choice: 5 points.
2nd choice: 3 points.
3rd choice: 1 point.

If it's a draw, then the same process will be undertaken except with only 1st and 2nd choice counting.

If it is still a draw: the winner of any category is the nomination with the most 1st choice votes. If two or more maps have the same amount of votes, then whichever of these maps has more second choice votes wins. The same goes for third choice if the category has a third choice vote allowance.
If they have the same amount of second choice or third choice (depending on the amount of choices for the category) votes, then a yet to be decided group of independant ejudicators will vote on who they think deserves to win.

If you didn't understand any of that, or have any questions, please ask. But don't worry about the voting system to much, if you don't understand it it doesn't really matter, only I really need to know the mechanics of it all. I just believed it was better to let everyone know how it will work.

I used to play photoshop tennis. Basically, it's where one person makes a picture, then another person edits the picture in an amusing way, then the next person edits the new picture in a new way and so on (ad infinitum).

Why can't we do this with maps?

The rules: you can edit the last map posted in whatever way you want, as long as you can still see parts of the previous map in your new map. You must post your new map in a txt file. You must never skip a map, and you don't need permission to post up a new one. You can change something very small, or the majority of the whole thing. Simple. #122569 3 2005-12-13T08:44:24Z sweep
Voting rules:

1) No voting for yourself.
2) No voting more than once per category choice.
3) If you wish to decline to vote in a category you may, and if you wish to decline to vote in a category choice.
4) If I wish to decline your votes, I will tell you so. I reserve the right to do this. I will only do it with very good reason, and it's unlikely it will have to happen. I might well tell people about it on this thread, to get a second opinion.
5) Please don't tell other people what you voted for. It ruins the fun. Of course, it's your secret, tell whoever you wish to, or hint at it, whatever, but it does ruin the fun; try to avoid it.
6) Don't throw pointed objects, you could have someone's eye out.

Vote counting system:

The choices are each worth thus:
1st choice: 5 points.
2nd choice: 3 points.
3rd choice: 1 point.

If it's a draw, then the same process will be undertaken except with only 1st and 2nd choice counting.

If it is still a draw: the winner of any category is the nomination with the most 1st choice votes. If two or more maps have the same amount of votes, then whichever of these maps has more second choice votes wins. The same goes for third choice if the category has a third choice vote allowance.
If they have the same amount of second choice or third choice (depending on the amount of choices for the category) votes, then a yet to be decided group of independant ejudicators will vote on who they think deserves to win.

If you didn't understand any of that, or have any questions, please ask. But don't worry about the voting system to much, if you don't understand it it doesn't really matter, only I really need to know the mechanics of it all. I just believed it was better to let everyone know how it will work.

Welcome to the world of bitesizeNUMA.

What is bitesizeNUMA?
It is a website containing links to maps on NUMA that community members with good judgement have deemed to be of a good quality.

How do I use bitesizeNUMA?
Click on a map thumbnail to open the map. The rest is pretty self-explanatory when it comes to general use.

How often will bitesizeNUMA be updated?
As soon as someone submits a map, it updates the website. Hopefully, people will be updating the website often, with mostly recent maps, but also older maps.

How do I add maps to bitesizeNUMA?
Only I can give you an account to do this. If you want one, just PM me about it, or email me at chimneysweepATgmailDOTcom. Whether you get an account or not is at my discrection, and if you don't get an account I will tell you why. You are perfectly at rights to appeal this decision, but I always have the final choice.

Final notes:
Please feel free to suggest features for the site, and please report any bugs you find. And if you see any abuse of the system, tell me and I'll sort it out.

I hope you enjoy it!

#124711 19 2005-12-19T17:12:44Z sweep
Music genres are useful, but you shouldn't depend on them to decide whether you like music or not.

Take, for example, pop music. Pop music is, by definition, music that is popular. Saying you don't like pop music is basically saying "regardless of the music quality, I will dislike music because it's popular, and this makes me feel anti-establishment and cool".

So, classify music all you want. It's useful. But ultimately, if someone suggests this "great band" and also says they're a "trip-hop, grungey alt. rap band" then it should be the "great band" part which forms your opinion on them before you've heard them.

#5802 1 2005-12-20T15:14:06Z sweep
There are two types of maps. Playable, and non-playable. Instead of non-playable counting for nothing, as great N-Art and great DDAs do take plenty of skill, there should be two seperate charts. Both in terms of authors and maps.

Authors Chart (playable)
Authors are ordered by who has the highest average rating achieved from 10 or more rated maps from the action, puzzle, race and survival categories.

Authors Chart (non-playable)
Authors are ordered by who has the highest average rating achieved from 10 or more rated maps from the n-art and DDA categories.

Map Chart (playable)
A chart of maps in order of rating from the action, puzzle, race and survival categories.

Map Chart (non-playable)
A chart of maps in order of rating from the n-art and DDA categories.

I fail to see any argument against this being implemented. It's logical, and will stop people complaining about n-art ending up at the top of the overall charts. They're two seperate types of map, it just makes sense to do this if you ask me.

The next thing she knows she's in a bath full of ice and has an incision in her abdomen. You smile, safe in the knowledge you now have 2 kidneys again. But what's this? A knocking at the door?

Really twisted. But I love it. Against the rules? Nah. That's staying!

#128583 4 2005-12-30T23:26:01Z sweep
Switch!


Highlight the white text below for spoiler:
Initially there is a 1/3 chance that the contestant picked the correct door. So, in this 1/3 of cases, switching doors will cause a loss.

However, in the 2/3 of cases where the contestant picked the incorrect door initially, the correct door is one of the two on the other side. Since the host always removes an incorrect door, switching in these 2/3 of cases always results in a win.
So... the probably is 1/3 for a win if you stay with your original pick versus 2/3 for a win if you switch.


It's hard to understand at first, but I came across this riddle a while ago in the excellent book "The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-time". Think about it hard, it makes perfect sense when you understand it.
