Quote
The two golden rules of web design:
1) Never change anything, people will always hate it
2) You can never please everyone.

Ok, so Arachnid asks me to make NUMA a logo. So, in three days, I spent a few hours each day toying with ideas. By the final day I had discovered what NUMA needed - a clean, simple, bold logo. Nothing more. Oh, and it needed to fit into the style of NUMA. That's why my final design was a run-of-the-mill, perpendicular, simple logo. This was where I made my first mistake. Arachnid was pleased with the logo, and he added it to the site. By this point I had idiotically gone ahead without taking heed of rule 1).

I had changed something. At this moment, the entire body of NUMA was angry.

<I'm about to express some opinions. These are honest opinions. If you don't like opinions, stop reading. Thankyou>

Then this happened. What the hell is that? You can't complain about the current logo then suggest that as a replacement.

And then this. I won't gloss it over, the bottom and top ones and awful. Awful. The middle one is good, but not really simple enough and harder to read when squeezed into the title bar.

And then this doozy. The top one is unreadable, and the bottom one... well, the U is just plain odd.

Then came some moderately alright ones. However, only the middle one seems in proportion. The other two should be discarded. The middle one... I'll vouch for that, it isn't bad. The only attempt I've seen by anyone that could make a good NUMA logo.

Cue these clever ones. Clever, yes, but hard to read. Therefore they wouldn't make good logos.

And most recently, there was this one. The top left one here is the only good one here, the other ones are awful. But reading that top left one belongs in the riddle thread, which rules that one out.


So, what be my point? Well, firstly, can you guys please stop moaning about the logo? It's perfectly fine as it is. If you want to design a new logo, that's fine, but please, actually take into consideration whether what you're doing would actually make a good logo or not. Secondly, think about why the logo was made to look how it looks. It's there for a reason, and it was built to fufill its needs. Before you make a logo, consider what those needs are.

Peace out.

/edit: Also, as a final note, try to remember that the tiles were made for level design, and not writing stuff. Therefore, I suggest that if you're going to make a logo you don't try and make it in Ned.

#131662 11 2006-01-11T16:13:08Z sweep
Blue, I don't disagree as such with your proportions. Infact, they're really pretty accurate. I just disagree that a rubric will work, because opinions on maps are so objective. Certain things outweigh other things, and certain puzzle maps have different formats.

You can't generalise action into one ratings system. The same with puzzles.

This is a nice system, but I'm sorry, I don't believe anyone should ever use it. People should form their own opinions. If anything, the following scale or something similar should be used as a guideline for playable maps:
0 - unplayable throughout
0.5 - mostly unplayable, playable parts unenjoyable
1 - mostly unplayable, playable parts enjoyable
1.5 - mostly playable, playable parts unenjoyable
2 - mostly playable, playable parts enjoyable
2.5 - playable, map is unenjoyable to play
3 - playable, map is indifferent to play
3.5 - playable, map is enjoyable to play
4 - playable, map is enjoyable to play and shows a well thought out design
4.5 - playable, map is highly enjoyable to play and shows a well thought out design
5 - playable, map is truly exceptional and enjoyable to play, and shows originality

This is just a quick draft of what I mean. I'm not going to do an unplayable one because I can't be bothered.

#6396 1 2006-01-23T17:54:40Z sweep
Many websites, such as last.fm and del.icio.us use a lovely tagging system. I think NUMA should have the same. Basically, people should be able to apply tags to maps. These tags could be "loopy", "fast", "puzzling jumper", "innovative" or anything you thought applied to the map. This would have two benefits. Firstly, people could search for maps that have certain tags. If I wanted, for example, to see some keep rocket alive DDAs I could search for maps with KRADDA in the tags. This would turn up all the KRADDA. I could also search for something like "challenging" or "complex".

Finally, this could improve the suggestions so much. Maps could be compared by tags. If you tended to favourite lots of maps with lasers in, the tags of these maps would include the word "laser" and as a result more maps with the tag "laser" would turn up in your suggestions.

Any thoughts?

Actually sweep this would be easy for code, i know a little about basic flash editing i do not know the codes for the game though but if its just an' enlargement angle as in scaling then you just need to add in a scale tile command

Never assume stuff like this. The fact is, curves are impossible, or at least that's what I've been led to believe.

You can't make bigger tiles than the ones that exist. And all tiles must have at least one of it's four grid edges completely covered by the tiles. This is due to the way it has been coded. A big curve, spilt into the size tiles we have now, would be impossible, because they wouldn't fill the grid properly.

And equally, as you can't make bigger tiles, making a big one isn't an option.

#6444 1 2006-01-25T20:18:02Z sweep
I had a big discussion/argument about this with a friend earlier today. I think it's false. My logic is simple, but not something my friend could quite quantify.

Currently, surgery exists that can advance your life span further than it takes longer to operate. For instance, a kindney transplant takes less than 24 hours, but will increase your life span (well, your predicted one) by potentially decades. If surgery such as this could be undertaken relatively often, then in theory this could keep happening and you'd live forever. Of course, at the moment this is impossible, but maybe in the future surgery or treatment would be created to combat old age...

Anyhoo, if you believe that treatment that could make you live forever is impossible, well, then the statement is incorrect anyway. Because then you're saying it's certain that this treatment will never be invented: in which case, the statement isn't correct, death isn't the one thing that is certain. The same thing applies to "you'll die when the universe ends" and so on.


You might not really be interested in what I just said, but I felt the urge to write it out and post it. Any thoughts?

#6859 1 2006-02-14T20:43:46Z sweep
I saw a real old sort-of documentary film in Geography last week. They compared a tribe of bushmen in who were at perfect piece with their environment with the city of Johannesburg just 50 miles away. There were loads of really fascinating things in it that had an affect on me, but there's only one part I'd like to share with you guys. When talking about why Johannesburg was so built up, it said something along these lines:
Quote
To save time, time-saving devices have been invented, and created in their millions. Although they were created to save time, people have just ended up doing more and more as a result of these machines, as they have to maintain and look after them. Children are even sentenced to 10 years of education just so they can survive in this harsh world of "time-saving" devices.

At this point, you're probably wondering why the hell I'm posting this in the NUMA discussion section. Well, my point is that it bears great relevance to NUMA.

The Bushmen are at peace with their environment. They look at what they've got, they don't complain, they live as a peaceful and happy environment. The people of Johannesburg, on the other hand, are constantly trying to improve but only making life harder for themselves in the process. The Bushmen are very contented, whilst the people of Johannesburg are unhappy and stressed. We need to learn to be at peace with our environment, NUMA, and work well as a community in it. There's nothing wrong with innovation, but we should stop looking to new features to solve our problems, and instead should try and fix the problems within the community by changing the way we behave.

I hope this doesn't go over everyone's head.

Right, I've gone through from 00-0 to 04-4, and I also played the two levels you mentioned. There were loads of really good maps in there, some especially fantastic, but what you really need to know about now is where things can be improved... so below I've highlighted things that might need improving. Bear in mind that I'm not as good at playing N as you probably are... so I'm a bit more sensitive to difficulty issues. I agree, however, with the feeling that these are possibly a little on the hard side.

00-0
Man, this takes a light touch... but I love it. That said, I wouldn't mind if you just nudged the exit switch up a tiny pixel or too... not sure how that would look asthesically though.

00-2
I found this incredibly hard.

00-3
I'm not sure of the tight squeeze in the middle. It's out of place from the rest of this map.

01-2
I know why you've done it, but once you start playing it the exit just looks offcenter. Not a major problem, but I thought I'd point it out.

02-1
One of my favourites. However, I can't help but feel that launchpad below the rocket should be either 1 or 1/2 tile lower. I can't land on it cleanly, because I keep on "hitting the roof" mid-jump.

03-2
I found this very hard.

03-3
The teleporter rocks, but if you're not going for all gold then it's really confusing. There needs to be something that makes you go to the launchpad...

09-4
It's a nice level. I feel a bit indifferent to it, but it does look good, and plays well enough. My only concern is the door switch towards the top right of the map placed directly above a mine in a one-tile high hallway. I've never been able to get passed a mine in that situation with much consistency at all, I think it'd piss a lot of people off.

10-4
Argh! You can do better than this. The four gauss combination is woefully annoying. It brings out the worst in gausses, in my opinion. There's just no escaping. The landscape on this level is nice, but I don't like the enemies you've used and how you've used them.

The task that was set...

The MiniMaps Contest

Judges:
Sweep
Lucidium
astheoceansblue (backup judge (judges any maps that judges submit))

At the beginning of time, man started to make stuff. Robots. Small cakes. Small robot cakes. Soon, man became bored with this process. He needed a change... and so, he just made everything smaller. Mini-robots. Mini small cakes. Mini small robot cakes. The process was an exciting one, and man found such a fascination in these mini creations that he continued making things smaller and smaller until he discovered that those tiny buttons on mobile phones are just not made for the fat human digits.

Anyhoo, that's neither here nor there. To the point.

There have been many classic maps for the game N over the past few years. Mount Doom springs to mind, as does Mother Thwumping Impossible and, naturally, the entirety of Yanu's collection. They may be classic, but they have one major flaw. They are not mini.

And so, this is your task: to recreate a map of your choice that we all know from NUMA, or the actual game itself, inside a map arena half the size of the one you're familiar to. This isn't simply about copying the map, it's about transferring and translating the gameplay and style to a smaller arena. Points are awarded for the difficulty of the challenge you take on, the extent to which you translated the gameplay and style to the smaller area, and generally how well the map plays.

Rules[/b]
- Most importantly, the minimap must be made within an area of 16 tiles wide by 12 tiles high.
- You can recreate any map that you want, but it must be either very widely known or on NUMA. If possible, you should provide a link to the map which you are mimicking.
- All entries must be submitted to NUMA, between the dates of 22nd of February and 21th of March
- It is your responsibilty to put "dibs" on doing a certain map. More than one of a particular map is allowed, the first submission may get more credit, depending on how similar the maps are.
- The map you mimic must not be your own.
- Maximum of 3 entries per person.
- The map should be entered as a Test Level unless the author of the original authorises you to do otherwise.

Judging[/b]
Each minimap is judged three times, each by a different judge. The criteria are as follows:
Translation quality/50 - the extent/quality of the similarity to the original map in terms of gameplay, feel, looks etc. Nothing more than half marks can be achieved if the map only looks like its predecessor.
Overall quality/25 - how good the minimap is, regardless of what it was trying to mimic.
Difficulty/25 - higher ratings are awarded for maps that the judge feels are harder to translate over to the smaller space.
Total/100
Overall Total/300

#7030 1 2006-02-24T14:29:40Z sweep
Please go through every step before starting your contest.


1) Are you doing this contest just because you want to do a contest, or is it because you believe you have a really great idea that would make a really enjoyable contest?
Only continue to 2) if you believe the answer is because you have a really great idea that would make a really enjoyable contest.
--------------------------
2) Is your the aim for your contest clear and simple?
Only continue to 3) if you believe the answer is yes.
--------------------------
3) Has your idea been done before in the same or a similar way?
Only continue to 4) if you believe the answer is no.
--------------------------
4) Have you drawn up a set of rules that are easy to follow and remember?
Only continue to 5) if you believe the answer is yes.
--------------------------
5) Is your judging system logical and as simple as possible?
Only continue to 6) if you believe the answer is yes.
--------------------------
6) Have you created a map for contest to test out the rules and judging scheme?
Only continue to 7) if you believe the answer is yes.
--------------------------
7) Do you really think people will enjoy making and playing maps for your contest?
Only continue to 8) if you believe the answer is yes.
--------------------------
8) Will you have enough time to maintain the entries list, the scores and the judging? Remember that it can be surprisingly time consuming.
Only continue to 9) if you believe the answer is yes.
--------------------------
9) Have you asked someone if they have any suggestions or thoughts for the contest?
Only continue to 10) if you have. If you haven't, feel free to ask in this thread so you can get a quality response.
--------------------------
10) Do you have any questions to ask before you start?
If the answer is no, start your contest. If the answer is yes, ask the question(s) in this thread.


This is just a provisional guide, there may be exceptions. Don't be afraid to ask questions, and please suggest any changes you think should be made to the above guide.

Mini Edgeplay by astheoceansblue

This felt quite a lot like the original, but not enough to warrant a +40 mark for translation. The top right was a bit crowded and not quite right, but the map as a whole was reasonably enjoyable to play for the most part. In terms of difficulty, the large open space in the middle of the original made translation a bit easier.

- Translation quality: 37/50
- Overall quality: 17/25
- Difficulty: 10/25
- Total: 64/100


Mini Quirkscrew by Krusch

Although asthesically this map doesn't look quite right, the fact is that it plays just like the original. It's exactly the same. Like Lucidium, I think the laser drone placement was a minor mistake, but I understand why the mines were excluded. Overall, this translation is excellent - it's just shame that it was really quite an easy one to make.

- Translation quality: 47/50
- Overall quality: 22/25
- Difficulty: 4/25
- Total: 73/100


Mini Mount Doom by Madnick

What I just don't understand is how you can put in so much effort in the looks but fail to place the chaingun drone so it stays within the mountain. In the original the chaingun drone doesn't venture far from the bottom right, but in yours it is exploring the whole map. This alone ruins this translation - you've changed the dynamics of one of the only two enemies completely! Anyway, this map, apart from that, is a bit hit and miss. Even asthesically, there is a general lack of attention to detail. Why's there a piece of gold under a mine? Where is there gold to the left of the trapdoor switch? Pah. I don't understand why you made these mistakes. But, credit where it's due, parts of it are pretty good. But overall... no, not good enough.

- Translation quality: 18/50
- Overall quality: 11/25
- Difficulty: 17/25
- Total: 46/100


Mini Just For You by chasethebase

This translation... makes me ever so slightly angry. Firstly, if the gold is causing problems with the launchpads then you either move the gold or use less! This contest isn't about just squeezing the objects together in a random fashion! It's about recreating the original map with careful thought and object placement. And this map... well, apart from looks, it barely resembles the original at all. Just feels like there was no thought put into it really. Forgetting about translation, it was reasonably fun to play.

Why have you done nothing about the bug-ridden one-ways at the bottom? Your placement of everything was such that the flow was completely lost. Moreover, if you're going to use as much space as you did (which you should really be because the original didn't use up all the vertical space) then use it to your advantage! My vote being the 5th vote, it revealed an average of 4.5/5.

I don't believe that NUMA members honestly like jumper puzzles that much. Although I'm not that good at N, I've been around for long enough to become pretty damn good in comparison to the majority of NUMA users. If I find most jumper puzzles hard and unenjoyable, I'd expect them to think the same.

I think it's a case of a mystical air surrounding these maps, a belief that they are some kind of fine art, a popular belief that everyone seems to share. As a result, anyone who doesn't enjoy playing them is too worried to give an honest rating, and just slaps a 4.5/5 on it.

People are no longer giving honest ratings. If you don't enjoy playing a map, then you shouldn't really be giving it a 4.5/5. The sheep of NUMA are following the crowd, and although fun maps get high ratings, the less enjoyable maps often seem to get high ratings on the basis of the myth surrounding them.

#164347 21 2006-04-13T08:33:59Z sweep
Ok, I should probably clarify on my points. Maps should be judged on what is applicable. In N Arts, you judge it on how good looks. People who say "meh, I look at it for 10 seconds and then get bored" and therefore give it a 2 - that's not valid. You're treated an N Art in comparison to an Action map, and they're just not the same thing.

However, puzzle maps are designed to be fun. That's the idea. I will rate one higher if it shows a greater degree of mapmaking skill, but ultimately I don't find them enjoyable. Puzzle maps belong to the genre of maps that is attempting to make you have fun, and therefore they should be rated as such. I appreciate some people enjoy them - then they can go ahead and rate them as such. But some people don't. They should rate honestly.

There's a reason the ratings system works on averages. This is something people seem to miss out. The idea is that you get the average opinion of the community, and if the community who don't like something are either muted or are pretending to like it then that's ruining the system. I know of several authors now that are creating jumper puzzle maps despite the fact that they don't enjoy playing them... I mean, that's completely ridiculous.

Also, in my original post I implied all jumpers are bad. That's not true, to be fair. There are a small number of jumpers that I love, and I do appreciate the worksmanship on others, but my point is that all of them seem to get 4.5/5 regardless of the fact that half the community doesn't find the majority of them fun at all. It doesn't make sense.

#8035 1 2006-04-13T20:17:54Z sweep
I'm going to post various music-based top tens. One at a time. Whenever I feel like it. Please agree/disagree, contribute, do whatever you want. I want to hear what you think, and most of all, if you're inspired by anything I write about a piece of music, go out and listen to it. I have an impeccable taste, honest.


Top Ten Songs With "Time" In The Title

10) Ben Scriven - Quality Time
This song is a bit silly. But it's number ten because it's silly.
/hindsight edit: And it has a kazoo solo. 'nuff said.

9) Hot Hot Heat - Running Out of Time
Vintage Hot Hot Heat; full of hooks, and over in the blink of an eye.

8) The Delays - Long Time Coming
What a wonderful little slice of music this is. It makes me all warm and fuzzy inside - it makes me think of family; I'm not sure why, but I like it!

7) U2 - Sometimes You Can't Make It On Your Own
It's remarkable that U2 are still a quality band after all these years. Sure, they haven't really done anything different, but their consistency is outstanding. This song is proof that they can still write brilliant songs.

6) Muse - Time Is Running Out
This is the best single Muse have ever written. It feels so electric and alive, and every time I hear it I am surprised about how I am yet to become bored of it.

5) Ben Scriven - Turn Back Time
Oh my. I just love the oriental instrumentation in this song coupled with the shamelessly unsubtle lyrics - "I can't comprehend how much I wish you were dead" is hardly poetry, but it works dammit. This song has groove, this song has feeling, and it has a wonderfully shameless instrumental climax.

4) Radiohead - We Suck Young Blood (Your Time Is Up)
This song is dark, dank and achingly gorgeous. The production is wonderful.

3) Semisonic - Closing Time
This song makes me happy. Very happy. I don't know whether it's because it evokes good memories, or whether it's darn good, but this song just makes me really happy.

2) Pink Floyd - Time
Unfortunately I'm a little too young to really be completely engrossed by the sound and feel of Pink Floyd, but this track is genius. Pure genius.

1) Green Day - Good Riddance (Time of Your Life)
This song is truly beautiful & honest; really pure songwriting.

That's the first top 10. As I said, comment as you wish. I want to hear what you think.

15)

13)

11)

6) National Anthem
This song rocks hard, but what I love most is the use of brass instruments - it's so anarchic, yet so perfect.

5) A Wolf At The Door (It Girl. Rag Doll)
Thom's voice is perfect in this, surely the best track of HTTT.

4) No Surprises
Oh my. It's just... well... I... oh my, it's just... yep, there we go, I'm crying. Bugger. I love this song.

3) Pyramid Song
This is an incredible song when you listen into it, but if you look at the actual technical side of the song it becomes phenomenal. When I listen to this, I can't help but close my eyes and immerse myself.

2) Street Spirit (Fade Out)
This is the song that originally got me into Radiohead, and ever since it has been one of my mainstay favourites. It's just so immersive, I could sit in a dark room, listen to this forever and never get bored.

1) Let Down
This song is perfection. Whenever and wherever I listen to it I just want to jump up and let out some kind of emphatic, triumphant, defiant tribal scream. This was one of the last songs on OK Computer to really hit me, but when it did I realised that I truly love it. It makes me want to cry tears of happiness.

Quote: great_sea, 2006-04-14T01:18:50Z
I like to compare this topic with music. If somebody doesn't enjoy country music, that doesn't mean the style itself is "bad." There are some very talented country artists who are not only skilled musicians, but are able to create music that appeals to alot of people (even if it doesn't appeal to me).

Now, the maps that I rate the highest are ones that I find enjoyable and "technically excellent." Beyond this, however, I will use moderation and give ratings based on not only how much I enjoyed a map; but also on the grounds of appearance, design, creativity, and public appeal.

This is very true, but once again I'd like to point out why the ratings system is designed the way it is. The idea is that you get an average of everyones opinions. Let's take some random figures: 50% of people love jumper puzzles, 40% of people like some jumper puzzles and 10% of people don't like any jumper puzzles.

Let's attach ratings to these people. Those who love jumper puzzles give 5/5 on average. Those who like some jumper puzzles give 3/5 on average. Those who don't like any give 1/5 on average. Now, let's figure out what this would give the average jumper puzzle:

5 +5
10 +5
15 +5
20 +5
25 +3
28 +3
31 +3
34 +3
37 +1
= 38
38/10 = 3.8 ninjas out of 5.

See my point? Things even out. There's a reason the ratings system works on averages. The ratings system is there to sift out the maps you will enjoy from the maps you don't enjoy. When you're on NUMA you don't go around looking for the most technically excellent map, we're not inspectors, we're looking for maps to have fun. If the (playable) maps aren't being rated on fun then the ratings system is pointless. Sure, a rating should also take innovation, aesthesics and technical brilliance into perspective but fun should usually come first and foremost in a playable map.

There are times, like Sendy's N Riddle where the design and innovation is so high that fun becomes dwarfed as a factor, but most of these jumper puzzles differ very little from each other, show little innovation from one another, and yet they're all getting 4.5/5.

I understand everything you guys have said, but I'd like you to realise that by rating the way you are rating you are making the ratings system even less worthwhile, as it is no longer truly doing its job. There are mapmakers constantly getting 4.5/5 that think they're are brilliant, but secretly at least half of NUMA doesn't enjoy their maps. IT MAKES NO SENSE.

Top Ten Songs Named After People

10 - Unintended (soft, fairly melancholic)
9 - Cave (nothing astounding, just good overall)
8 - The Small Print (good rock)
7 - Hyper Music (great beat and chorus)
6 - Falling Away With You (quite soft for much of it)

2 - Citizen Erased (epic, 7 minutes long, in four distinct [but still cohesive] sections)
1 - New Born (experimental enough to be interesting without being pretentious]

Plug In Baby (it's all in the riff and the beat)
Thoughts Of A Dying Atheist (the title alone is enough)
Apocalypse Please (not the best song on it's own, but a great opener for the album)
Showbiz
Stockholm Syndrome
OK Computer and Kid A are my two favourites. I couldn't pick between them, they're so very different. OK Computer is more accessible and every track could be brilliant when isolated, whereas with Kid A it's the whole journey, how it all fits together, one or two tracks wouldn't work when isolated.

Next I'd place Amnesiac and the Bends (both ace albums, but just simply not as good as Kid A and OK C), shortly followed by Hail To The Thief, which is undeservedly underrated IMO. Then Pablo Honey, which is pretty poor but with some good songs in nonetheless. And, coming later this year is LP7 which could be freaking brilliant. #165883 48 2006-04-17T20:59:00Z sweep
Quote: maestro, April 17, 2006 06:12 pm
As promised, here is my Franz Ferdinand Top 10. It was far easier for me to write comments for this one than on my Muse Top 10.

1. Darts of Pleasure - This is the song that got me hooked on Franz Ferdinand. I can get caught up in the beat so easily, and the whole song just bounces on it. The lyrics are also quite distinctive: you've got "you can feel my lips undress your eyes", and the song ends with three repetitions of a verse in German.
2. You Could Have It So Much Better - A song that is both bright and cynical. I love the lyrics, an inspecific rejection of the accepted order and an equally inspecific call to arms .
3. The Fallen - Lots of biblical allusions in the lyrics that I don't quite get, especially in the breathtaking final chorus.
4. Your Diary - This song doesn't deserve to be a a B-side. The chorus is great (musically, not so much lyrically), and the guitar riffage throughout this song is also excellent.
5. This Fire - Can't really say much about this one. It's... good?
6. Auf Achse - This song is a combination of many different musical stylessort-of-romantic background notes, a disco-y beat, a dance-y beat, and the great choruswhich just manage to form a cohesive song.
This starts off with a romantic sounding intro, and then an almost disco-y beat comes in, giving it a strange vibe. Combined with the chorus, this makes a great song.
7. Take Me Out - A tragically and ridiculously overplayed song, but a fairly good one nevertheless.
8. 40' - It would appear that Franz Ferdinand got writer's block on this song, explaining the two dozen repetitions of "la la la la". A good song nevertheless.
9. Outsiders - Twangy guitars, something that sounds a lot like those weird plastic toy tubes that make a whiny, warbling sound when you turn them upside down, and a drum beat that doesn't change for the entire song.
10. Jacqueline / Eleanor Put Your Boots On - I can't decide. Jacequeline is a more typical song, while Eleanor Put Your Boots On is a much softer song. Call this a tie.

IMO This Boy is missing from that list. 40' is also my favourite Franz song. There's something just so wonderful about it - you call the "lalalala" bit lazy, I think it's genius. It suits the mood.

The PS3 is going to be dropped like a dead fish by the majority of consumers. Sony seem to be progressively digging a bigger and bigger whole for themselves.

Firstly
Wii = 150/$250
PS3 = 425/$399
If my memory serves my correctly the XBox flopped at launch, and a lot of that was down to its extortianate price. Sony seem hell bent on including blu-ray technology in the PS3 - and this has blown the price out of the water. Experts predict the console will cost $494 to make; Sony will be at a loss of $105 for every sale. The console is so expensive, and has priced out a huge amount of consumers. Couple this with the Wii being wonderfully cheap, and it's clear that Sony are screwed.

Secondly
PS3 has Blu-ray...
Wii has innovation
Let's see. Blu-ray is far more expensive. Many games console consumers probably don't even know what it is. Nintendo's innovatory controller (which, as discovered the other day, also doubles up as a microphone) is looking the push the boundaries of gaming, creates an incredibly intuitive feel and is visually a great selling point. It'll be hard to advertise using Blu-ray, it just isn't visual enough. The Wii's controller will look great when advertised.
Er, basically, the Wii controller improves the Wii more than Blu-ray will improve the PS3, it is cheaper than Blu-ray, and the Wii controller is born for marketing whereas Blu-ray will just come across as phony business speak.

Thirdly
Sony don't care about their customers
In a move that parallels DRM in the music world (which there recently has been a huge backlash against) Sony look likely to make second-hand disc use impossible. This will piss consumers off. Simple.

I don't know which muppet is making the decisions for Sony at the moment, but I think Nintendo are going to wipe the floor with them. Recently there was a poll asking which console was currently most wanted - PS3 came out at number 1. When push comes to shove, I have a feeling consumers, especially the ones strapped for cash, are going to opt for the innovatory Wii over the overpriced, unimaginative PS3.

#9157 1 2006-05-31T16:56:22Z sweep
Version 3 is here! What's changed?
- The website now runs with a fully-fledged login system, that means you don't have to enter your username and password everytime you submit a map.
- More importantly though, thanks to the magic of "bookmarklets" and the expertise of the legend that is Arachnid, you can now submit maps straight from NUMA. It requires a few steps for you to set-up, but doesn't take long at all. To find out how to do this and, er, "unleash your map submitting power", take a gander at this page which should tell you everything you need to know.

For those of you that aren't members, nothing has really changed for you, but hopefully the login system and bookmarklet mean we will see more maps submitted to bitesizeNUMA, which is rather dandy, don't ya think?

Quote: Introduction to bitesizeNUMA
Welcome to the world of bitesizeNUMA.

What is bitesizeNUMA?
It is a website containing links to maps on NUMA that community members with good judgement have deemed to be of a good quality.

How do I use bitesizeNUMA?
Click on a map thumbnail to open the map. The rest is pretty self-explanatory when it comes to general use.

How often will bitesizeNUMA be updated?
As soon as someone submits a map, it updates the website. Hopefully, people will be updating the website often, with mostly recent maps, but also older maps.

How do I add maps to bitesizeNUMA?
Only I can give you an account to do this. If you want one, just PM me about it, or email me at chimneysweepATgmailDOTcom. Whether you get an account or not is at my discrection, and if you don't get an account I will tell you why. You are perfectly at rights to appeal this decision, but I always have the final choice.

Final notes:
Please feel free to suggest features for the site, and please report any bugs you find. And if you see any abuse of the system, tell me and I'll sort it out.

I hope you enjoy it!

I've had an idea for a nation vs. nation knock-out or possibly league tournament.

It'll encorporate both map making and highscoring. It probably won't launch until July, but I'd like to get an idea of the number of countries entering so I can build the format around it.

Basically, everyone is gonna team up as their home-nations. Four people per nation. Two map-makers, two highscorers. Some nations will have too many people for this format, such as maybe the USA, in which case we'll split it South & North or something. Other nations may not have enough, in which case nations will be combined, as appropriately as possible (eg, Germany and Austria go together). Also, nations are allowed to use substitutes if they decide that's easiest for them.

Each nation also needs a leader.

So, if you guys could say if you're interested, state your nation, and possibly mention anyone else that you know from your nation that could be interested. Oh, and to clarify, this should be the nation you either live in or were born in or belong to in some very strong way.

#185115 72 2006-06-05T19:32:07Z sweep
1) Start of round. Task is set to mapmakers (eg, create a map without tiles)
2) Mapmakers create their maps and submit them within a set deadline. Mapmakers must stipulate whether the highscorers must all-gold their map or not.
3) Highscorers have a week to get the lowest overall framecount of all four maps added together.
4) At the end of this week points are given accordingly to the highscorers.
5) Each other nation ranks the maps, and points are given accordingly.
6) Huttah! Match done. If we do this in knock-out form, the team with the highest points progress. In the event of a draw, a vote over which should progress is taken. If this is done in league form, then it's 3 points for a win, 1 for a draw.

How does that sound?

#196787 5 2006-06-30T09:12:28Z sweep
Descriptions not yet put up (I'll do that once inductees are confirmed)

Coalition by LittleViking001 (written by KA)
If Convention is the epitome of littleviking001's map-making, Coalition is its sequel, the pinnacle of this great author's illustrious career. M&R included it in N 1.4 for its incredible likeness to a Metanet-authored venture, with its amazing use of tileset versatility, object placement, and multiple enemies, sans clash; coalition is a true extravaganza, and will be cemented in history as one of the community's favourite maps.
"Excellent! Another masterpiece!" (Kablizzy)

Desperado by jeffkililan
The beauty of Jeffkillian's Deseperado is that without playing it would be easy to dismiss as another run-of-the-mill bounceblock/rocket map. However, once you begin bounding about with your ninja this level comes to life - some say Desperado is the perfect action map, and it is very, very hard to find a good reason to disagree with that opinion.
"Great map... the epitome of rocket/bounceblock action" (krusch)

Fossil by Zorn
You would be hard pressed to find a better map asthesically than Zorn's eyepopping masterpiece Fossil. The Hall of Fame could never be complete without a classic Zorn map, and this is about as good as it gets. Visually stunning, fun to play, and stylish beyond belief, Fossil is a simply a classic.
"Great tileset, fun gameplay, perfect difficulty." (Red Reamer)

Twisted by Killisk
Twisted by Killisk is proof that a great map doesn't need any enemies - gravity does the job just as well. Based on a perplexing labrynth of unusual tile arrangements that make navigation harder than you expect, Twisted is a puzzle stripped down to the bare bones - quite simply superb.
"Best map ever... I heart this soooooo much" (joem)

Advanced Robotics by tktktk
Advanced Robotics by tktktk is a prisoner style map that runs on a vast, traffic-like network of drones. Level 76-4 of the Legacy Project, Advanced Robotics is yet another reason why tktktk is seen as such a talented author - style, with substance.
"I love this... one of my faves" (krusch)

Edgeplay by Sendy
It looks like a playpark, but, in reality Sendy's Edgeplay is a pure action map based on the premise of navigating around the edge of the map. The entire map only has one enemy: the rocket in the center. So simple, so effective, so very brilliant.
"This is really fantastic. The varied styles, the 'high flying' aspect... this is the type of map I'd love to make, but I can never quite get down." (stepself)

Valves by Lucidium
Valves by Lucidium is stylish, innovative, elegent and altogether puzzling. Taking advantage of both a floorguard bug and the way a floorguard interacts with the ninja, Lucidium created a simple but very effective puzzle - and ended up with a faultless, intruiging map.
"Brilliant idea, perfectly executed. 5 ninjas." (tktktk)

domo-kun ftw!! by krusch
Australian map-maker krusch's domo-kun FTW!! is an undeniably brilliant slice of minimalistic action, fused with krusch's downright sexy style. Each and every enemy is used to great effect; everything is just so damn perfect.
"This is gold. Let me put it to you this way: one of my favorite maps ever. No. Kidding." (Baraba)

Flight by maximo
When a map is one of an author's best, it is generally a good sign. When a map is one of maximo's best, it's an absolutely fanfrickingtastic sign. Flight is addictive and great fun, even by maximo's standards; full of open space, Flight is a quintessential action map, a level of legend.
"By far one of the best maps I have ever seen. I'm 100% in love with it." (tktktk)

Bubble Point by stepself
Bubble Point is yet another visually stunning map from the community treasure that is stepself (voted author the year in 2005). Simple but effective drone paths decorate the mine-ridden landscape - Bubble Point is a map to remember.
"Brilliantly crafted" (Baraba)

I found an interesting page for foul play statistics. It take the number of dives, tantrums, referee bullying instances, fake injuries, yellow cards and red cards, and weighs it with the number of games each nation played at this World Cup.
Quote: Formula for IBI Foul Play Index
Yellow Cards * 1pt + Red Cards * 2pts + Bully Ref * 4pts + Dives * 4pts + Fake Injury *4pts + Tantrums * 2pts divided by Number of Games

Here are the nations of this world cup, sorted by the IBI Foul Play Index (the worse a nation is, the higher the IBI Foul Play Index) on the basis of this World Cup...


You can find the whole page at http://www.informationbuilders.co.uk/ONTHEBALL/wcuk.htm

Of course, this isn't perfect, but I think it does make interesting interpretation. There are no huge surprises, apart from maybe how low Argentina are. I didn't expect Italy to be *quite* as high as that, as against Germany there was no foul play going on, but I suppose they were up to their usual tricks earlier inthe tournament.

There was a decent bbc article on this earlier today, below is a version with the boring bits removed:
Quote: http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_cup_2006/5169342.stm
Materazzi defended himself on Tuesday in the Italian newspaper La Gazetta dello Sport, when he said: "It was the kind of insult you will hear dozens of times and just slips out of the ground.

"I didn't call Zidane a terrorist and certainly didn't mention his mother."

But Materazzi added: "I am ignorant, I don't even know what an Islamic terrorist is; my only terrorist is her," he said pointing to his 10-month-old daughter.

"I did not bring up Zidane's mother; for me a mother is sacred."

"I held his shirt, for only a few seconds," said Materazzi, who had scored Italy's equaliser after Zidane put France ahead from the penalty spot.

"He turned towards me and scoffed at me, looking at me with super arrogance, up and down.

"He said 'if you really want my shirt, you can have it later.'

"It's true, I shot back with an insult."

Media organisations across Europe have been trying to decipher what Materazzi said to provoke such an extreme reaction from Zidane.

But it remains unclear exactly what was said and the BBC has broadcast two different versions.

BBC Radio Five Live asked for help from a deaf lip reader, Jessica Rees, who read the words phonetically to an Italian translator.

She deciphered the insult as being "you're the son of a terrorist whore" - a translation also carried by many national newspapers in Britain on Tuesday.

The BBC's Ten O'Clock News also called in experts to study the television footage of the incident and determined the following:

Materazzi's first word to Zidane was "no" before he then told him to "calm down".

He then accused him of being a "liar" and wished "an ugly death to you and your family" on the day the Frenchman's mother had been taken to hospital ill. This was followed by "Go f*** yourself".

Zidane's agent, Alain Migliaccio, has hinted that Zidane will soon reveal exactly what was said by Materazzi.

#201635 64 2006-07-12T09:13:21Z sweep
Now, don't get me wrong, he's an incredible player. But Zidane didn't deserve the golden ball - with or without the headcharge incident.

Let's go through his World Cup.

France 0-0 Switzerland
Zidane was anonymous, he also got a yellow card.
Quote: BBC Sport
France captain Zinedine Zidane was not his usual inspirational self
France 1-1 South Korea
Zidane was decent, very quiet by "golden ball" standards, and received another yellow card - ruling him out against Togo.
Quote: BBC Sport
Zinedine Zidane was then booked for France and will now miss the third match, possibly bringing down the curtain on his career in a way he could never have envisaged.
Togo 0-2 France
Zidane was suspended, so he didn't play. Luckily for Zidane, his team bailed him out of a dissapointing career end with a 2-0 win against France.

Spain 1-3 France
Zidane's first good performance. He was a key part of this match, and capped it off with a well taken goal at the end. He was yellow carded once again though, and if he hadn't scored the goal it would have been seen as a waste of a chance.
Quote: BBC Sport
Zidane, who struggled in France's first two group games, looks to have finally found his rhythm
Brazil 0-1 France
He was fricking fantastic. This was his performance of the tournament.
Quote: BBC Sport
Zidane was magnificent throughout
Portugal 0-1 France
He scored a penalty. Not particularly a sign that a player is world-class. Zizou's performance in this match was decent, but nothing special.
Quote: BBC Sport
Zidane's influence on proceedings was not quite as substantial as in the previous rounds against Spain or Brazil
Italy 1-1 France (Italy win 5-3 on penalties)
Zidane was lucky to find his penalty go in (it only just crossed the line, any higher and it wouldn't have, he definitely wasn't trying to skirt the line that much). Elsewhere, he was decent once again. Oh, and he got sent off for a head-charge against Materazzi.
Quote: BBC Sport
Playing his last game before retiring, Zinedine Zidane's career ended in disgrace after he was sent off for crazily headbutting Marco Materazzi.

So, there was only one match where he was superb, one where he was good, two where he was decent, one where he was anonymous and one where he disgraced himself. The form of the golden ball player? Surely not. What about Canavarro, who was consistently brilliant throughout the tournament? Or, if you're adverse to giving it to a defender, what about Pirlo, for his consistent brilliance throughout?

Zidane? You're having a laugh. If you're giving it on the basis of one performance, why not give it to Owen Hargreaves for his unbelievable performance against Portugal?

He hasn't lost all respect, he will still be remembered as an incredible player, but the fact he's won the golden ball is inexplicable.

#207017 4 2006-07-25T11:20:12Z sweep
A website requires to be easily accessible by accident for the searchbots. Let me go through the general process of my understanding of it.

1) You put the webpage up. This page contains two words - "egg" and "yuppy" (this is a bit random, but there's a reason why I've specified this). Furthermore, you have specified two meta tag keywords - "island" and "mongoose". So, you upload this webpage to the internet. So far, so good.

2) The webpage remains on the internet, but there are no links on other webpages to it, or, there are links but on pages which aren't linked themselves. Searchbots can't track down pages if they don't have links, they won't try random letter combinations to see if certain pages exist, they just follow the internet's large link chain. So, at this point, no bots find you, and you are not on Google.

3) BAM! You're finally linked. On a website already monitored by Google, they link to your website. The link text is "tree" (random again, but I'm coming to this). So, the bots follow the link to your site, and record what your page has on it. Immeadiately, it records "egg" and "yuppy" as words on your page, "island" and "mongoose" as meta tags and "tree" as a word strongly. These words are then how your site can be found on Google - and every time someone links to you, they are adding words for this purpose, if they all use similar words, the effect is multiplied. If you get 50,000 people linking you with the word "tree" then you'll be very high under the search "tree" - the words on your page of course bear an influence, as do the metatags.

You can also directly link the bots to your page with the link iangb just gave - it's akin to another page with a link to yours.

For the record, the way you're linked does have a very strong effect, and this is best demonstrated by the number one result on Google for searching "failure" - it comes up with a biography of George W. Bush. This is because people decided it would be funny to make this happen, so they all linked to that page with the link text "failure".

#10395 1 2006-08-01T14:06:05Z sweep
I've been thinking about this idea for a while, just in the context of games in general, and, personally, I think it could make things really exciting. Furthermore, I realised it could apply to N - and I don't think it would really ruin any of the "classic" feel of N, but merely create a new, exciting gameplay element. Also, it would provide an alternative to one-ways and trapdoors.

Anyway, the actual idea. I've made a set of 5 images below to demonstrate the idea.

Basically, the idea is that you can connect any pair parrallel walls (that directly face each other) with a green laser. This laser does not harm the ninja, it is more along the lines of a switch. When the ninja crosses the laser, the laser turns blue and the walls close in on each other. Any enemies of objects "consumed" by the wall would be crushed too.

The main point of it is to create the excitement of having to leave rooms before they basically vanish with you in them. Imagine the excitement

Here is what I'm demonstrating in the images below:

Fig. 1A: The basic setup before the laser has been crossed.
Fig. 1B: The laser has just been crossed. It has turned blue to show this, and the walls have started closing in - note that the wall is doing more of a growing action, so it's not moving as a whole, it's just closing in from the inside.
Fig. 1C: Our sorry ninja has made a dash for the exit, but the corridor is closing in on him, and he's about to be crushed just before he makes it to freedom. Once again, note that the wall is doing more of a growing action, so it's not moving as a whole (all tiles connected stay in the same position), it's just closing in from the inside.

Fig. 2: Another example where the laser could be used.

Fig. 3: Another example where the laser could be used.
Attachment (lost): post-8-1154441165.jpg

#221565 8 2006-08-30T09:16:52Z sweep
This is an interesting idea, but I fear it'd be _very_ hard to do.

DDAs are about precision. Because there is no user input as such, this precision is possible. It's not so much a problem that human error exists, it's human error over time that's the worry. Say, with one mistake you're 5 frames off. Then you're 1 on the next, spot on the next, then 2, 3, 0, 1, 6, 2. By the end of that you've made 20 frames of error from just a few jumps. It builds up, and in a DDA precision is so important.

I think it's possible, but I also think it'd be very hard to make one with loads of close-calls in that was actually reasonably possible to complete.

#236365 52 2006-10-02T17:36:06Z sweep
Talk about missunderstanding/misrepresenting an idea.

The idea of a waiting period before you could start submitting and voting has two benefits. Firstly, it means snipers, who will often be sniping in the spur of the moment, are less likely to be active as they have to be patient to be able to snipe. It eliminates the hot-headed snipers from the equation, reducing the total to only the premeditated ones.

The second point is that it encourages them to spend the 10 days observing other mapmakers. A lot of mapmakers are bad because they don't play other people's maps and so they just don't understand what the point of mapmaking really is.

Mind you, I'm not sure the idea I suggested was a ten day period of not being able to submit maps, I think it was ten days of not being able to vote. Either way, it has potential.

#240935 23 2006-10-14T09:14:11Z sweep
Social conditioning does shape people (to both be rebels and to be "good") but I think what are more interesting are the situational factors that cause someone to act in a certain way at a certain time. I know that's similar to social conditioning, but I'm talking in the moment as opposed to over a long period of time.

Milgram got people to apply increasingly powerful electric shocks (up to fatal @ 450 volts) to fellow test volunteers next door - with the person next door screaming to let them out, and then finally going silent to imply they were dead (the shocks weren't real, the stress was recorded, but the people applying the shocks were not to know). Some of the people applying fatal shocks continued and continued but were so under stress they had seizures. Milgram pressured them to continue, the lab situation at Yale University made them scared to stop, and the contract they had signed was one they were reluctant to break. So 65% of people became so irrational they went all the way up to 450 volts, a fatal "dosage", while everyone went to 350 volts.

They were all informed of the effect of the shocks. But they all became pretty damn evil. But it was entirely because of the situation. Social influences have far more effect than anything else.

Quote: Tsukatu, October 14, 2006 10:11 pm
I don't think that most people who have anything better than a TI-82 fully deserve them. I have a TI-83+, and I've learned just about every facet of its functionality, with the exception of some boring finance/statistical commands that I never bothered to learn. I've made Yahtzee and Battleship with full GUI's in BASIC. I can do more with my TI-83+ than any of my classmates who have a better model. It just doesn't benefit you, and you may as well go with a more basic model if you're not using it for something as advanced.
I cringe when I hear some freshmen brag about having TI-89's for their geometry classes. Even a TI-82 will have more than they'll ever use throughout their high school years, and probably a year or two into college (and it could be all they'd ever need if they're not majoring or minoring in math or a technical science).
If you're using a TI-83+, a TI-84, TI-86, or TI-89 as a frickin' scientific calculator, you've blown a ridiculous amount of money. The TI-82 is a very, very powerful device and likely has more than you'll ever need, but people love big numbers. Higher model numbers are just insane new features for math majors. How many of you people with TI-89's actually use their 3D graphing functions? Do you even know what a derivative or an integral is (which the TI-82 handles just dandily)?

If you're interested in games, save money by getting a TI-82 and a gameboy. Don't disgrace a TI-89 Titanium by using it for trigonometry and games.

#12188 1 2006-11-10T10:56:08Z sweep
I'm the youngest of five boys. Growing up, I always felt like was a blessing. My older brothers have always led by example, and I've always been mature beyond my years as a direct result (in my opinion) of the examples my brothers have set.

But, unfortunately, it's not that simple. And part of the problem is that I have excelled far to easily for my own good in some cases. This is an arrogant statement, but forced modesty is more arrogant, and I'm not going to lie just to make you guys think I don't have a high opinion of myself. I am academically and socially successful, I'm creative but analytical at the same time, I breeze past things in the way others can't. I'm not someone that works painstakingly to do well, I just do well. By all accounts, my life should be brilliant. But this ease has come back to haunt me. Where all my brothers have been successful academically, I have managed to follow - but where my brothers have been successful in certain areas, I have somehow pooled all those areas and been successful in pretty much every one.

I know what you're thinking: "fuck you. Your life sounds great. How is your self-proclaimed success a problem?" Well, that's what I might have said if I was you. But as I said, it's not that simple.

When you become so good at following the success of four older brothers, you feel like you have to follow what they've achieved. In many cases this isn't a problem, but when it comes to love, it is. Each of my brothers found someone they fell in love with around about my age. The sad truth is that not all those relationships have lasted - but they were still great relationships. The problem for me is that I've spent the last five years of my life building up to this moment in time, expecting to find someone and fall in love with them. I want to madly fall for someone, and I want them to madly fall for me.

But, heck, it hasn't happened. Probably because I'm only 17. But in my mind, I'm scared shitless. I have great friends, which I maintain great friendships with, but I feel lonely. Very lonely. Within myself I am possessed with following the path - leading the same life my brothers have led before me, but the truth is, it can't work like that. I'm a logical person. I'm aware of this. But no matter how much I tell myself that it doesn't matter about where I am, inside I will always be burning until I find someone.

And to make things more confusing, this deep desire to find that special person makes liking anyone difficult. In the past week there's someone - who will remain unnamed - who I like. She's a very touchy-feely person, and we get along well, but she gets along well with so many people. By all rights, I should just like her and see how things go from there. But in my mind it's nowhere near that simple. I know I only like her, but because I'm so desperate inside to love someone I spend all day thinking about her, and the smallest interaction to her can send me into an incredibly good mood for the rest of the day or - and these happen 50/50 btw - she can send me into a deep depression for the rest of the day.

Now I've hit a three-day weekend. Yesterday was a day of depression. I know this will carry over through today, Saturday and Sunday. Great. I won't be able to be productive because I'll spend all my time staring into space and feeling shit about someone that I do like - but not that much - and she's also pretty completely different from me. In my mind, if we were to start a relationship, I honestly don't see the dynamics. But for some reason, my instincts do. And it's fucking me up inside.

This is only one week in. I'm scared. This feels like it will control me indefinitely. I love the highs - but the rest is just awful. I feel like I know where I am logically, but my instincts can't follow this logic - and I am completely and utterly caught up with this person. Which just makes me feel so incredibly lonely.

If you've read all of the above, thank you. I appreciate it. That's a lot of self-absorbed crap you've just trawled through. Please, if you have any comments, I want to here them.

/edit: Here's something to add. Early this morning (about three AM) I stood still for two hours in my room listening to music that makes me feel... supernatural, I guess. I had the window open. It was freezing. I chose not to close it for the whole two hours. It felt like I was going insane at the time. But I'm not sure if I was just putting it on. Once the music stop I collapsed on my bed and fell asleep immediately.

This is another feeling I know well, though perhaps in a different guise. I'm intelligent, witty, and I have tonnes of important stories to tell. I'm certainly not unnattractive and I'm not afraid to get close to someone. And yet, I know tonnes of shallow idiots with nothing to them that seem far too popular. How the hell isn't that me? Maybe it's because I think it should be.

Quote: Tsukatu, 2006-11-10T12:06:00Z
When I first saw how my life was differing from my brother's, I began to develop a serious, though amusing in retrospect, identity issue. I didn't understand why I wasn't falling in love as he was. There were some girls in my class that would have complemented my personality very well, and they certainly had their middle-school crushes on me (a series of stories brutally summarized into a self-indulgent but nevertheless accurate statement - 90% of the girls in any academic class I've been in since 3rd grade have been head-over-heels for me at some point in time; this is backed up by countless testimonials, mostly in yearbooks), and I always felt really guilty that I didn't feel anything for them.
So I started trying to.
This hits the spot. I don't know whether I like this girl because I like her or because I feel like I should like her anymore. If I was fully rational, I have no idea whether I'd be even talking to her often at all anymore.

Quote: Tsukatu, 2006-11-10T12:06:00Z
A lot more stupid shit happened, and I started doing irrational things like you've described. I spent hours walking in my backyard in my boxers in the middle of a freezing winter night, I pondered my identity over some lukewarm tea out on a balcony in the rain, and contemplated the nature of love in the fetal position in the back of my closet. I did all sorts of wierd shit like that. My mind was mostly on why I wasn't feeling anything for people, whether I should, who felt what for me... most of it ended up being meaningless.
I want to say something about this section of text. But I don't know what to add. Perhaps I just want to say that for me it all revolves around music. I ritually spend a good half an hour each night just listening to music and dancing around like a maniac at the moment. It lifts me up, it drops me down, it makes me feel, as I said, supernatural. Last night was different because I just stood there. I've wanted - especially in the past month - someone that I can dance like a maniac to music with, a companion that would do it with me, that would completely let go with me. Maybe it's symbolic that I was motionless.

Quote: Tsukatu, 2006-11-10T12:06:00Z

Quote: Obby, 2006-11-11T05:10:58Z
Quote: Kablizzy, 2006-11-11T04:12:00Z
Alongside Suki, and yourself, I can identify in an otherworldly sense with all of this.
Was that directed at me?
Nope, it was directed at me.

----------

But, aside from where the conversation is directing in this thread, I feel I've moved on a step since I posted here yesterday. I know where I am now. Last night I was up till 6am talking about life with some of my closest friends.

I still feel highly strung about the whole situation, but I don't think it matters. I thought this weekend was going to be shit, but I already feel on top of the world again. One thing that came from last night is that the stigma with telling people how you feel is bullshit. You guys seem to be quite keen to advise me not to necessarily tell her how I feel, because of some sort of impending crisis that could happen if she rejected me. The truth is, I shouldn't be afraid to tell her.

If I tell her, and she reciprocates it, fantastic.

If I tell her, and she doesn't reciprocate it immediately, she will think about it over time, and I know plenty of people that have only fallen for someone as a result of them knowing they were liked in the first place.

Let's say she doesn't reciprocate it, and never will. If you've told her early on, you'll move on from it. The more you don't tell her and she finds out some other way, it becomes an issue and being friends is impossible.

I've spent so much of the past week analysing what she does and I've been all over the shop as a result. I should just tell her. Perhaps I should get to know her a bit better first (and I will, because I know I'd be shitting bricks if I tried to tell her now) but I now know it's not worth making the mistake of hiding feelings.

#267279 14 2006-12-09T22:32:12Z sweep
Quote: blue_tetris, December 09, 2006 11:16 pm
Here my two cents:

Nearly all NUMA users rate maps normally (4's, mostly) until the public rating appears.  When the public rating appears, people have one of two thoughts:

"That rating is too high" or "That rating is too low".

If the rating is too high, you rate lower than the map to reduce the rating.  The lower that you rate it, the more powerful your rating is.  Why rate anything other than a zero if you'd want to reduce the rating?  If you want your rating to have its highest possible effect, you'd rate it a zero.  (The reverse is true for fives; if you want it up, you'll rate it a five to have the biggest possible effect.)

I'm saying that the standard user's thought-process lends itself to a binary rating system.  It is the number of users who rate a map that provides numerical data.  Individual users will surely want to maximize their effect on a map.

Again: Individuals act upon binary decisions.  These decisions, en mass, amount to numerical data.
Alternatively, you just tell them how they should be voting. People used to vote pretty accurately back in the day, because the average was more around 3.

Each value you can vote should be assigned to a degree of how much the user likes the map. That way people are also all voting on the same terms. People are only voting binary because there's nothing to suggest it's not the right thing to do. Believe it or not, if you teach people the right thing, they generally follow it.

#267490 21 2006-12-10T10:20:55Z sweep
Quote: blue_tetris, December 10, 2006 12:16 am
I've always considered the idea of "vote disparity". It uses the existing rating system.

Basically, any time you vote on a map that already has 5 votes (and is displayed publicly), it tallies the absolute difference by which you vote differs from the average. For instance, if the map has a rating of 3.8 after five votes and you rate it a 1.5, you receive a "vote disparity" of 2.3. Conversely, if a map has a rating of 2.7 and you give it a 4.5, you receive a "vote disparity" of 1.8.

These vote disparities are registered and an average is rendered (total vote disparity / total number of votes). A user with a high vote disparity might be less than trustworthy in voting. These vote disparities would only be viewable to sweep, maestro, and perhaps any bitesizers. The would be a way to search the database for risk behavior--by showing the members in order of vote disparity (high to low). This system would be to reveal snipers.

Also, histograms. Just: histograms. I'm sure that's almost a given.



Another really good suggestion (): a system that automatically compares the IPs of registering users to users who already exist to give reports as to risky users. For instance:

(c=a given number; *=a boolean variable)

If two or more users have c.c.c.c, then the risk of multiaccounting is given as "very high" for those users.
If two or more users have c.c.c.*, then the risk is "high".
If two or more users have c.c.*.*, then the risk is "moderate".

This quick, automatically-generating data will allow the operators (sweep and maestro) to more readily detect problematic users. Sweep and maestro could re-sort the database of users to show the highest risk users at the top. Evidently, this system would reveal multiaccounters. It's possible that there could even be a way to compare the voting behaviors of the "very high" and "high" risk users, to give a percentage of how many of their recent votes (within 24 hours) are the same numbers on the same maps.

I think you're over-thinking what is in essence a simple problem.

#267528 4 2006-12-10T12:04:19Z sweep
It's worth thinking about, but there are probably better ways around the problem. Let me illustrate something though, to show you why median isn't entirely appropriate.

Hypothetical situation:
You have five ratings, on what is essentially a terrible map. It receives two ratings from experienced members, who recognize this, giving it 0 and 0.5. Transversely, three relatively new members, including one who is good friends of the guy who posted the map, give the level 4.5, another 4.5, and 5.
The result? Median would judge the rating of this map as 4.5. The current system would give this map a rating of 3.1. The map deserves nothing more than 1, really... and median is so way off it's not even a joke.

#12944 1 2006-12-17T16:23:29Z sweep
In the past 24 hours, as I'm sure anyone that has spent any time browsing the forums is probably aware, a huge number of multi-accounters have come out of the woodwork, confessing to what they've done.

Whilst some people have found this pretty shocking, I'm not really surprised. We all knew that there were multi-accounters amongst us, we just didn't really know the extent. Earlier today maestro spent quite some time analyzing the votes in the NUMA database and has since identified four more well-known members that he suspects of partaking in multi-accounting fraud. We are following this up, and we will continue to see if we can expose any more cheats from the system.

Whilst it is fantastic that so many people are coming clean, this has made something clear: the system is inherently flawed. The way NUMA is constructed has allowed this to happen.

Here are some of the essential problems with the system:
  • The focus of the website is placed too strongly on ratings. If you want to browse maps and want to avoid the poor stuff, you'll head straight for the top rated charts. We want browsing NUMA to be different - you should be able to find maps by difficulty, tags, favorites and bitesizing. Being able to search by ratings is brilliant, but it sends out the wrong message - it makes people think that ratings are the be all and end all. Well, they shouldn't be the be all. Or the end all.
  • People aren't scared of being caught. Whilst Arachnid was in charge, he wasn't actively searching out multi-accounters. That's fair enough, he's a busy man, but it meant that anyone who wasn't a bit low in the brain cell department could easily cheat the system to their benefit. People need to know that they will be caught. Systems need to be in place to detect vote fraud.
  • People who commit vote fraud and get away with it find swaying the average rating of maps very easy to do. A single 0 on a map with four existing ratings of 5 has the effect of dropping the average rating by 4. There are ways round this: namely histograms and mechanisms to discard outliers automatically.
NUMA needs work. It needs restructuring. This is all very possible. We have ideas, we have plans, maestro has smarts and I have more solutions than we could ever need.

But something bugs me particularly. Discovering that so many people have been multi-accounting (pending even more likely additions to the list in the near future) has spelt it out loud and clear: all voting that has been made since the beginning of NUMA is corrupted. Every single map that has seen the top rated page very probably has some kind of suspicious activity in its records. I hate this. I hate the idea that there are traces of these crimes throughout every nook and cranny of NUMA, and I am keen to start over.

What I want to suggest is by no means certain. It's just something I wanted to throw out there, and something that maestro is keen to hear the community's response to. I know a lot of people may react badly to it. I am open to hearing what you guys think. My suggestion is drastic, and at the moment just a potential road that we've pondered.

I want to wipe the slate clean. I want to reset all the voting on NUMA, removing every vote from the system. No exceptions. See it as a detox. Washing all the crap out of the system. Starting again.

If we were to do this, we wouldn't completely discard the old ratings - we would save all the old average ratings to the database, so people could browse via that and all the voting of the past isn't completely wasted. Equally, the resetting of the votes would be done alongside introducing measures to solve the flaws in the system mentioned above. We would change the focus of the website, and start over again.

If you hate the idea, we want to hear it. We want to hear what you think we should do instead. If you love the idea, we want to hear your response too.

Quote: maximo, 2007-01-23T05:36:50Z
First off ratings: anyone with half a brain knows not to care about ratings because they mean so little about actual map quality, so my question is simply why keep them? The system I think would work (better/more efficiently/what have you) is a simple thumbs up. If after playing a map you enjoyed it, give it a "Yay" (as I'll refer to it from now on), if not, do nothing (more on "do nothing" later). the amount of Yay's a map has correlates directly to the number of people who have enjoyed the map enough to recommend it to other players, or at least the people who think the map is worth looking at.

Now in addition to that there should be in my opinion a thumbs down (or "Nay") option. This isn't to say you didn't like the map, but that it was horrendous and not worth playing, this isn't a button for "i didn't like this map" it's for "this map is horrible/noobish/spam/etc." more on how I feel this should work in the next section. For maps you don't care for, or just didn't really enjoy, you do nothing.
This system already pretty much exists, barring the "nay". It's called favorites. And in fact, at one point Arachnid removed ratings and turned the way maps were ranked by the percentage of people that have favorited the given map. Guess what? The community rejected it. It had potential, but the community moaned about it so much that it wasn't worth it anymore.
The benefits of a scale from 0-5 are clear. Why should my opinion boil down to a yes or a no, when there's much more to it? Why exchange the "rich" data system we have now for a binary one? I understand why you thought of it, but I'd much rather reach perfection with the current system than surrender and downgrade ourselves.

Quote: maximo, 2007-01-23T05:36:50Z
Top rated pages next: Obviously this screws the hell out of the current system based of highest scores and percentages. I think the new table should work as follows though. The top rated page is broken into 3 categories: past week, past month, and all time (with the possibility of past 24 hours if deemed appropriate). The maps with the most Yay's for the given time block are listed in descending order. This in my oppinion gives the advantage of a frequently changing top authors page, giving new authors a chance to be seen, and letting numa cycle and be more fluid than it is now (Mount Doom is still up there). Although Mount Doom is probably worthy of the spot, when you are surfing for new maps seeing a 2 year old map isn't want you want to see quickly. This allows quicker scanning of numa and a higher chance new authors will be recognized (or at least in theory).
Having top rated broken down into past week, month and all time is genius. I fully approve of that part of the concept.

Quote: maximo, 2007-01-23T05:36:50Z

This could be shortened to 6 months or maybe even 3 and make it a quarterly honor (author of the season maybe) so it cycles more often.

I can't argue the fact that old maps will get lost in the shuffle.  Just brainstorming, possibly link to the old top rated pages so people remember to go back and vote.  Just freeze them and still allow access to them so people can still see and vote on them without going back 2 years into the databases.
Nick's old system was shot down because people didn't like how it didn't really cover for maps that you quite liked but not enough to favourite. Any binary-type system (which your proposal is virtually) will have this flaw.

I agree that the ratings system has caused a lot of problems. We need to change the focus. We need to bring in map tagging (oh come on, that'll just be awesome!) and have top rated charts also organised by favorites, and bring in histograms, and... you get the idea. We don't need to get rid of ratings. We just need to stop them from being the be-all-and-end-all, change the focus of the website. Right now, if you want to browse maps, you head for the top rated without much hesitation. We want you to be using different techniques - we want the recommendation system to be more useful. We want bitesize to be more useful, and actually part of NUMA. We want you to be able to search tags - searching "abstract" and "puzzle" would bring up abstract puzzles. You're no longer browsing by rating, but just using it as a factor for choosing what to play.

You see where I'm going with this?

#14279 1 2007-03-03T11:39:08Z sweep
If you know what MetaSecret is, skip to below the line. If you don't know, here's a quick explanation:
MetaSecret is a community project where people sent in secrets of theirs, anonymously. That pretty much describes it. It's that simple. It is based on the brilliant Post Secret, of course.
_____________________________________________________________________________

Firstly, thanks to everyone who participated. This project completely, 100%, relied on the community to make it great. You guys did a great job.

The way I have presented the secrets was an attempt to give all the secrets their own personality, and make it feel like they were coming from different people. I think that if they were all the same font etc then it would have seemed a bit odd. Because I chose a bigger font for a secret does not mean I think it's more important - in fact, some of the ones I made really small were my favorites. It was just an effective way of doing things, and you should read every secret as carefully as the last.

The secrets are not in any order, chronological or anything. They were pretty randomly ordered.

I did edit selected secrets for grammar. I also made minor edits where appropriate. There was an instance where someone submitted an image which just wouldn't fit in so I turned it to text. And there were a few secrets that I have not included, for a variety of reasons - a few were clearly just jokes, whilst one mentioned hatred towards forum members; this was clearly not appropriate for this project.

There was one instance where someone, by choice included their name at the end of their secret so people could contact them if they felt they were going through a similar situation. I decided to remove it, as it isn't within the spirit of the project presentation, but if they wish to say which secret is theirs in this thread then that's perfectly fine.

Please discuss this project. Obviously, we don't want speculation about who submitted what. But apart from that, discuss away... in this thread, or even start a new one if there's a secret which really hit you hard.

I hope you guys find this as moving to read as I found to compile it.

MetaSecret

Mirror
